sentences.zh: 黃庭堅 晁補之弟:詠之 秦觀 張耒 陳師道 李廌 劉恕 王無咎 蔡肇 李格非 呂南公 郭祥正 米芾 劉詵 倪濤 李公麟 周邦彥 朱長文 劉弇

translations.literal: Huang Tingjian, Chao Buzhi's younger cousin Yongzhi, Qin Guan, Zhang Lei, Chen Shidao, Li Zhi, Liu Shu, Wang Wujiu, Cai Zhao, Li Gefei, Lu Nangong, Guo Xiangzheng, Mi Fei, Liu Shen, Ni Tao, Li Gonglin, Zhou Bangyan, Zhu Changwen, Liu Yan
translations.idiomatic: Huang Tingjian; Chao Buzhi's younger cousin Yongzhi; Qin Guan; Zhang Lei; Chen Shidao; Li Zhi; Liu Shu; Wang Wujiu; Cai Zhao; Li Gefei; Lu Nangong; Guo Xiangzheng; Mi Fei; Liu Shen; Ni Tao; Li Gonglin; Zhou Bangyan; Zhu Changwen; and Liu Yan

sentences.zh: 黃庭堅

translations.literal: Huang Tingjian
translations.idiomatic: Huang Tingjian

sentences.zh: 黃庭堅字魯直，洪州分寧人。

translations.literal: Huang Tingjian, style name Luzhi, was a native of Fenning in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Tingjian, whose style name was Luzhi, came from Fenning in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼警悟，讀書數過輒成誦。

translations.literal: In childhood he was quick and perceptive; after reading a text several times he could recite it from memory.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was exceptionally quick-witted; a few readings of any book were enough for him to recite it by heart.

sentences.zh: 舅李常過其家，取架上書問之，無不通，常驚，以為一日千里。

translations.literal: His uncle Li Chang visited the family, took books from the shelf and questioned him on them — there was none he did not understand. Chang was astonished and thought his progress was a thousand li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Li Chang called at the house, he would take books from the shelf and quiz him; there was not one Huang could not answer. Chang marveled, saying the boy advanced a thousand li in a single day.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調葉縣尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate's assistant of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was posted as magistrate's assistant in Ye County.

sentences.zh: 熙甯初，舉四京學官，第文為優，教授北京國子監，留守文彥博才之，留再任。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era he was selected as an academic officer of the Four Capitals; his literary composition ranked highest. He was appointed instructor at the Northern Capital Directorate of Education. The regional commissioner Wen Yanbo recognized his talent and had him retained for a second term.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining reign he was chosen as an academic officer for the Four Capitals and placed first in the literary examination. He taught at the Northern Capital Directorate of Education, and the regional commissioner Wen Yanbo, impressed by his ability, kept him on for a second term.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾嘗見其詩文，以為超軼絕塵，獨立萬物之表，世久無此作，由是聲名始震。

translations.literal: Su Shi once saw his poetry and prose and thought them transcendent beyond the dust, standing alone above all things; the age had long lacked such work, and from this his reputation first shook the world.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi read his poetry and prose, he judged them to soar far above the common run, standing alone beyond all comparison — works the age had not seen in years — and from that moment Huang's fame began to resound.

sentences.zh: 知太和縣，以平易治。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Taihe County he governed with simplicity and ease.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Taihe County, he governed in an unassuming, even-handed way.

sentences.zh: 時課頒鹽筴，諸縣爭占多數，太和獨否，吏不悅，而民安之。

translations.literal: At the time salt quotas were issued as a tax assessment; the counties vied to claim inflated figures, but Taihe alone refused. The clerks were displeased, yet the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When salt-tax quotas were handed down, every county rushed to report inflated figures; Taihe alone declined. The clerks were unhappy, but the people were relieved.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，召為校書郎、《神宗實錄》檢討官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, he was summoned as collator and reviser of the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhezong took the throne, Huang was summoned as collator and reviser for the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong.

sentences.zh: 逾年，遷著作佐郎，加集賢校理。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to assistant compiler and additionally made collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted to assistant compiler and given the additional post of collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 《實錄》成，擢起居舍人。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records were completed, he was promoted to attendant in the Office for Recording the Emperor's Actions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records were finished, he was promoted to attendant in the Office for Recording the Emperor's Actions.

sentences.zh: 丁母艱。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 庭堅性篤孝，母病彌年，晝夜視顏色，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: Tingjian was by nature deeply filial. When his mother was ill for more than a year, day and night he watched her complexion and did not loosen his belt.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was profoundly filial by nature. During his mother's illness, which lasted more than a year, he watched her face day and night and never undressed for bed.

sentences.zh: 及亡，廬墓下，哀毀得疾幾殆。

translations.literal: When she died he built a hut by the grave and mourned so grievously that he fell ill and nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he kept vigil at the tomb; his grief was so extreme that he fell gravely ill and nearly died.

sentences.zh: 服除，為秘書丞，提點明道宮兼國史編修官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became secretary of the Palace Library, commissioner of the Mingdao Palace, and concurrently compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was made secretary of the Palace Library, put in charge of the Mingdao Palace, and appointed compiler of the national history as well.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，出知宣州，改鄂州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era he was sent out as prefect of Xuanzhou and then transferred to Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaosheng reign he was sent out to serve as prefect of Xuanzhou, then reassigned to Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 章惇、蔡卞與其黨論《實錄》多誣，俾前史官分居畿邑以待問，摘千餘條示之，謂為無驗證。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun, Cai Bian, and their faction argued that the Veritable Records contained much slander. They had the former historiographers dispersed to towns around the capital to await interrogation, selected more than a thousand entries to show them, and declared them unsubstantiated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun, Cai Bian, and their allies claimed the Veritable Records were full of slander. Former historiographers were scattered to towns around the capital to await questioning; more than a thousand passages were singled out and pronounced unsupported.

sentences.zh: 既而院吏考閱，悉有據依，所餘才三十二事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the academy clerks examined them and found that all had documentary basis; only thirty-two items remained in dispute.
translations.idiomatic: When academy clerks reviewed the charges, every entry proved to have documentary support; only thirty-two items were left in question.

sentences.zh: 庭堅書「用鐵龍爪治河，有同兒戲」，至是首問焉。

translations.literal: Tingjian had written, "Using iron dragon claws to control the river is like child's play," and now this was the first matter questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Huang had written that "using iron dragon claws to control the Yellow River was child's play," and this was now the first charge put to him.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「庭堅時官北都，嘗親見之，真兒戲耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "When Tingjian was an official at the Northern Capital I personally witnessed it — it truly was child's play."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "When I served at the Northern Capital I saw it with my own eyes — it really was child's play."

sentences.zh: 凡有問，皆直辭以對，聞者壯之。

translations.literal: Whenever he was questioned he answered with blunt forthrightness, and those who heard were heartened.
translations.idiomatic: To every question he gave a blunt, forthright answer, and those who heard him were heartened.

sentences.zh: 貶涪州別駕、黔州安置，言者猶以處善地為法。

translations.literal: He was demoted to vice-prefect of Fuzhou and settled at Qianzhou; critics still objected that he was placed in too favorable a region.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to vice-prefect of Fuzhou and exiled to Qianzhou, yet his critics still complained that the place was too mild a punishment.

sentences.zh: 以親嫌，遂移戎州。

translations.literal: Because of a conflict of kinship interest, he was then moved to Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On grounds of a kinship conflict of interest, he was transferred to Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 庭堅泊然，不以遷謫介意。

translations.literal: Tingjian remained tranquil and did not mind banishment or demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Huang remained serene and took no account of his exile or demotion.

sentences.zh: 蜀士慕從之遊，講學不倦，凡經指授，下筆皆可觀。

translations.literal: Scholars of Shu admired him and followed him to study; he lectured tirelessly, and whatever he had instructed, their written work was all worth reading.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan scholars flocked to study with him. He lectured without tiring, and whatever he had taught them, their compositions were invariably worth reading.

sentences.zh: 庭堅學問文章，天成性得，陳師道謂其詩得法杜甫，學甫而不為者。

translations.literal: Tingjian's learning and literary works were gifts of innate endowment. Chen Shidao said his poetry had mastered Du Fu's method — he studied Fu without merely imitating him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang's scholarship and writing seemed gifts of nature itself. Chen Shidao said his poetry had mastered Du Fu's method — he learned from Du Fu without becoming a mere imitator.

sentences.zh: 善行、草書，楷法亦自成一家。

translations.literal: He excelled at running and cursive script; his regular script also formed a school of its own.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in running and cursive script, and his regular script likewise formed a school of its own.

sentences.zh: 與張耒、晁補之、秦觀俱游蘇軾門，天下稱為四學士，而庭堅于文章尤長於詩，蜀、江西君子以庭堅配軾，故稱「蘇、黃」。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Lei, Chao Buzhi, and Qin Guan he studied under Su Shi; the realm called them the Four Academicians. Among them Tingjian was especially accomplished in poetry. Gentlemen of Shu and Jiangxi paired Tingjian with Shi, hence the name "Su and Huang."
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhang Lei, Chao Buzhi, and Qin Guan he studied under Su Shi, and the world called them the Four Academicians. Huang was especially renowned for poetry; scholars in Shu and Jiangxi ranked him alongside Su Shi, whence the pairing "Su and Huang."

sentences.zh: 軾為侍從時，舉以自代，其詞有「瑰偉之文，妙絕當世，孝友之行，追配古人」之語，其重之也如此。

translations.literal: When Shi was in attendance at court he recommended him to succeed himself, with words such as "magnificent writings unsurpassed in the age, filial and brotherly conduct matching the ancients" — such was the weight he gave him.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at court, Su Shi recommended him as his own successor, writing that his "magnificent prose was unmatched in the age" and his "filial and brotherly conduct rivaled the ancients" — such was the esteem in which Su held him.

sentences.zh: 初，遊灊皖山谷寺、石牛洞，樂其林泉之勝，因自號山谷道人雲。

translations.literal: Earlier he had visited the Valley Temple and Stone Ox Cave in Qian and Wan, delighted by their forest springs and scenic beauty, and therefore styled himself the Daoist of the Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he visited the Valley Temple and Stone Ox Cave in the Qian-Wan region, charmed by their woods and springs, and took for himself the sobriquet Daoist of the Valley.

sentences.zh: 晁補之

translations.literal: Chao Buzhi
translations.idiomatic: Chao Buzhi

sentences.zh: 晁補之，字無咎，濟州钜野人，太子少傅迥五世孫，宗愨之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Chao Buzhi, style name Wujiu, was a native of Juye in Jizhou, fifth-generation descendant of the Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Chao Jiong and great-grandson of Zong Que.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Buzhi, whose style name was Wujiu, came from Juye in Jizhou — a fifth-generation descendant of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Chao Jiong and great-grandson of Zong Que.

sentences.zh: 父端友，工于詩。

translations.literal: His father Duanyou was skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duanyou was accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 補之聰敏強記，才解事即善屬文，王安國一見奇之。

translations.literal: Buzhi was clever, quick to remember, and as soon as he could understand affairs he was adept at composition. Wang Anguo marveled at him on first meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhi was quick-witted with a formidable memory; as soon as he could grasp affairs he wrote well. Wang Anguo was astonished at first sight.

sentences.zh: 十七歲從父官杭州，稡錢塘山川風物之麗，著《七述》以謁州通判蘇軾。

translations.literal: At seventeen he followed his father to an office in Hangzhou, gathered the beauty of Qiantang's mountains, rivers, and scenery, and composed the "Seven Accounts" to present to the vice-prefect Su Shi.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he accompanied his father to Hangzhou, gathered material on the splendors of Qiantang's landscape, and wrote the "Seven Accounts" to present to Vice-Prefect Su Shi.

sentences.zh: 軾先欲有所賦，讀之歎曰：「吾可以閣筆矣！」

translations.literal: Shi had first intended to compose something himself; after reading it he sighed and said, "I may put away my brush!"
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi had meant to write something of his own first; after reading it he sighed and said, "I can put away my brush!"

sentences.zh: 又稱其文博辯雋偉，絕人遠甚，必顯於世。

translations.literal: He also praised his writing as learned, eloquent, and lofty, far surpassing others, certain to shine in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared that Buzhi's writing was learned, eloquent, and magnificent — far beyond ordinary men — and that he was bound to make his mark in the world.

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: From this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: From that time his name spread.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，試開封及禮部別院，皆第一。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, taking first place in both the Kaifeng and Ministry of Rites special examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and placed first in both the Kaifeng and Ministry of Rites qualifying rounds.

sentences.zh: 神宗閱其文曰：「是深於經術者，可革浮薄。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong read his essay and said, "This is one deeply versed in the classics — he can reform shallow frivolity."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong read his examination essay and said, "Here is a man deeply grounded in the classics — he can help cure the age of its shallowness."

sentences.zh: 調澶州司戶參軍，北京國子監教授。

translations.literal: He was appointed revenue section aide of Danzhou and instructor at the Northern Capital Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as revenue aide in Danzhou and appointed instructor at the Northern Capital Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，為太學正，李清臣薦堪館閣，召試，除秘書省正字，遷校書郎，以秘閣校理通判揚州，召還，為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was director of the Imperial University. Li Qingchen recommended him as fit for the palace archives; summoned for examination, he was made rectifier of texts in the Secretariat, then transferred to collator, and as collator of the Secret Archive served as vice-prefect of Yangzhou. Recalled, he became assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou reign he served as director of the Imperial University. Li Qingchen recommended him for the palace archives; after a court examination he was made rectifier of texts, then collator, and as Secret Archive collator he served as vice-prefect of Yangzhou. Recalled to the capital, he was made assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 章惇當國，出知齊州，群盜晝掠途巷。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun held power he was sent out as prefect of Qizhou, where bandits plundered the streets in broad daylight.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun dominated the government, Buzhi was sent out as prefect of Qizhou, where gangs of robbers looted the streets even in daylight.

sentences.zh: 補之默得其姓名、囊橐皆審，一日宴客，召賊曹以方略授之，酒行未竟，悉擒以來，一府為徹警。

translations.literal: Buzhi had quietly obtained their names and verified their loot in detail. One day while entertaining guests he summoned the bandit-catchers, gave them his plan, and before the wine round had finished all were seized and brought in; the whole prefecture was thoroughly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhi had quietly identified every robber by name and traced their spoils. One day at a banquet he called in the bandit-catchers, gave them his plan, and before the wine had made a full round every culprit was seized; the whole prefecture was shaken.

sentences.zh: 坐修《神宗實錄》失實，降通判應天府、亳州，又貶監處、信二州酒稅。

translations.literal: Because of inaccuracies in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong, he was demoted to vice-prefect of Yingtianfu and Bozhou, then further demoted to supervise the wine tax of Chuzhou and Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Charged with inaccuracies in the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong, he was demoted to vice-prefect of Yingtianfu and Bozhou, then reduced to supervising the wine tax in Chuzhou and Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，復以著作召。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, he was again summoned as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, he was summoned back as compiler.

sentences.zh: 既至，拜吏部員外郎、禮部郎中，兼國史編修、實錄檢討官。

translations.literal: Once he arrived he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Personnel and bureau director of the Ministry of Rites, concurrently compiler of the national history and reviser of the veritable records.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was made vice director in the Ministry of Personnel and bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, while also serving as national-history compiler and veritable-records reviser.

sentences.zh: 黨論起，為諫官管師仁所論，出知河中府，修河橋以便民，民畫祠其像。

translations.literal: When factional accusations arose he was impeached by remonstrance official Guan Shiren and sent out as prefect of Hezhongfu. He repaired river bridges for the people's convenience, and the people painted his image in shrines.
translations.idiomatic: When the factional purges began, remonstrance official Guan Shiren denounced him and he was sent out as prefect of Hezhongfu. He rebuilt river bridges to ease travel, and the people set up painted portraits of him in shrines.

sentences.zh: 徙湖州、密州、果州，遂主管鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Huzhou, Mizhou, and Guozhou, then put in charge of the Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved through Huzhou, Mizhou, and Guozhou, then placed in charge of the Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 還家，葺歸來園，自號歸來子，忘情仕進，慕陶潛為人。

translations.literal: Returning home he built the Garden of Return and styled himself the Returned One, indifferent to official advancement and admiring Tao Qian's character.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he laid out the Garden of Return, called himself the Returned One, put career ambition aside, and took Tao Qian as his model.

sentences.zh: 大觀末，出黨籍，起知達州，改泗州，卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: Late in the Daguan era he was removed from the proscribed faction list, recalled as prefect of Dazhou, transferred to Sizhou, and died at the age of fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daguan reign he was cleared from the faction blacklist, recalled to serve as prefect of Dazhou, transferred to Sizhou, and died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 補之才氣飄逸，嗜學不知倦，文章溫潤典縟，其淩麗奇卓出於天成。

translations.literal: Buzhi's talent was buoyant and free; he loved learning without weariness. His prose was warm, polished, and ornate; its soaring brilliance and strangeness sprang from innate endowment.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhi's spirit was buoyant and free, and he studied tirelessly. His prose was warm, polished, and richly patterned; its soaring brilliance seemed a gift of nature.

sentences.zh: 尤精《楚詞》，論集屈、宋以來賦詠為《變離騷》等三書。

translations.literal: He was especially expert in the Songs of Chu, gathering fu and lyric poetry from Qu Yuan and Song Yu onward into three works including Transformations of the Lisao.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially masterful in the Songs of Chu and compiled fu and lyric poetry from Qu Yuan and Song Yu onward into three books, including Transformations of the Lisao.

sentences.zh: 安南用兵，著《罪言》一篇，大意欲擇仁厚勇略吏為五管郡守，及修海上諸郡武備，議者以為通達世務。

translations.literal: When Annan was at war he wrote an essay "Words of Blame," whose main idea was to select officials of benevolence, courage, and strategy as prefects of the Five Circuits and to strengthen coastal defenses — critics thought it showed mastery of worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the war in Annan he wrote an essay called "Words of Blame," arguing that benevolent yet bold officials should govern the Five Circuits and that coastal defenses must be strengthened. Commentators judged it proof of his grasp of practical statecraft.

sentences.zh: 從弟詠之。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Yongzhi.

sentences.zh: 弟 詠之

translations.literal: Younger brother Yongzhi
translations.idiomatic: Younger Cousin Yongzhi

sentences.zh: 詠之字之道，少有異材，以蔭入官。

translations.literal: Yongzhi, style name Zhidao, had unusual talent in youth and entered office by hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi, whose style name was Zhidao, showed unusual gifts early and entered office through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 調揚州司法參軍，未上。

translations.literal: He was appointed judicial aide of Yangzhou but had not yet taken up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial aide in Yangzhou but had not yet reported for duty.

sentences.zh: 時蘇軾守揚州，補之倅州事，以其詩文獻軾，軾曰：「有才如此，獨不令我一識面邪？」

translations.literal: At the time Su Shi was prefect of Yangzhou and Buzhi assisted in prefectural affairs. Buzhi presented Yongzhi's poetry and prose to Shi, who said, "With talent like this, will you not even let me meet him?"
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi was then prefect of Yangzhou, with Buzhi assisting in prefectural affairs. Buzhi showed him Yongzhi's writings, and Su Shi said, "Talent like this — and you won't even let me meet the man?"

sentences.zh: 乃具參軍禮入謁，軾下堂挽而上，顧坐客曰：「奇才也！」

translations.literal: He then arranged the formal visit of a judicial aide. Shi came down from the hall to take his arm and lead him up, then turned to the seated guests and said, "A rare genius!"
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi was presented in formal aide's dress. Su Shi came down from the hall, took his arm, and escorted him up, then told the guests, "Here is a rare genius!"

sentences.zh: 復舉進士，又舉宏詞，一時傳誦其文。

translations.literal: He again passed the jinshi examination and also passed the macro-elocution examination; for a time his writings were read and recited everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination again and also the macro-elocution examination, and for a time his essays were on everyone's lips.

sentences.zh: 為河中教授，元符末，應詔上書論事，罷官。

translations.literal: He served as instructor in Hezhong. Late in the Yuanfu era, in response to an imperial edict he submitted a memorial discussing affairs and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He taught in Hezhong. Late in the Yuanfu reign he answered an imperial call with a memorial on public affairs and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，為京兆府司錄事，秩滿，提點崇福宮，卒，年五十二，有文集五十卷。

translations.literal: After a long interval he became recorder of the Metropolitan Prefecture. When his term ended he was put in charge of the Chongfu Palace and died at fifty-two, leaving a collected works in fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he became recorder of the Metropolitan Prefecture. When his term ended he was placed in charge of the Chongfu Palace; he died at fifty-two, leaving collected works in fifty juan.

sentences.zh: 秦觀，字少遊，一字太虛，揚州高郵人。

translations.literal: Qin Guan, style name Shaoyou, also styled Taixu, was a native of Gaoyou in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Guan, whose style names were Shaoyou and Taixu, came from Gaoyou in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少豪雋，慷慨溢於文詞，舉進士不中。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and brilliant; his generous spirit overflowed in his writings. He failed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and brilliant, his passionate spirit pouring into his writing. He failed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 強志盛氣，好大而見奇，讀兵家書與己意合。

translations.literal: His will was strong and his spirit high; he loved grand designs and sought the extraordinary. Reading military texts, he found them in accord with his own mind.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious and high-spirited, he loved grand designs and the extraordinary. When he read military classics, they matched his own temperament.

sentences.zh: 見蘇軾于徐，為賦黃樓，軾以為有屈、宋才。

translations.literal: He met Su Shi at Xuzhou and composed a fu on the Yellow Tower. Shi thought he had the talent of Qu Yuan and Song Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He met Su Shi at Xuzhou and wrote a fu on the Yellow Tower; Su Shi judged him the equal of Qu Yuan and Song Yu.

sentences.zh: 又介其詩于王安石，安石亦謂清新似鮑、謝。

translations.literal: He also introduced his poetry to Wang Anshi, who likewise said it was fresh and clear like Bao Zhao and Xie Lingyun.
translations.idiomatic: He also introduced his poetry to Wang Anshi, who likewise praised its freshness, comparing it to Bao Zhao and Xie Lingyun.

sentences.zh: 軾勉以應舉為親養，始登第，調定海主簿、蔡州教授。

translations.literal: Shi urged him to take the examinations to support his parents, and he finally passed, appointed registrar of Dinghai and instructor of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi urged him to sit for the examinations so he could support his parents; he finally passed and was posted as registrar in Dinghai and instructor in Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，軾以賢良方正薦於朝，除太學博士，校正秘書省書籍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era Shi recommended him to the court as worthy and upright; he was made erudite of the Imperial University and corrector of books in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou reign Su Shi recommended him to court as a worthy and upright scholar; he was made erudite of the Imperial University and corrector of Secretariat books.

sentences.zh: 遷正字，而復為兼國史院編修官，上日有硯墨器幣之賜。

translations.literal: He was transferred to rectifier of texts and again served concurrently as compiler in the National History Academy; on court days he received gifts of inkstones, ink, vessels, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to rectifier of texts and again served as compiler in the National History Academy; on days when he attended court he received gifts of inkstones, ink, vessels, and silks.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，坐黨籍，出通判杭州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era, because of the faction list he was sent out as vice-prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaosheng reign he was listed among the faction and sent out as vice-prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以御史劉拯論其增損實錄，貶監處州酒稅。

translations.literal: Because censor Liu Cheng accused him of altering the veritable records, he was demoted to supervise the wine tax of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Cheng charged him with tampering with the veritable records, and he was demoted to supervising the wine tax in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 使者承風望指，候伺過失，既而無所得，則以謁告寫佛書為罪，削秩徙郴州，繼編管橫州，又徙雷州。

translations.literal: Envoys followed the prevailing wind and watched for faults. Finding none, they then charged him with copying Buddhist scriptures while on leave, stripped his rank and moved him to Chenzhou, then placed him under restricted supervision at Hengzhou, and again transferred him to Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys followed the political wind and watched for any slip. When they found none, they charged him with copying Buddhist scriptures on personal leave, stripped his rank, and exiled him to Chenzhou, then placed him under restricted supervision at Hengzhou, and finally moved him to Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，復宣德郎，放還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, he was restored to Gentleman for Promoting Virtue and released to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, he was restored to Gentleman for Promoting Virtue and allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 至藤州，出遊華光亭，為客道夢中長短句，索水欲飲，水至，笑視之而卒。

translations.literal: Reaching Tengzhou, he went out to visit the Huaguang Pavilion, told his guests ci verses from a dream, asked for water to drink; when the water came he smiled, looked at it, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Tengzhou he visited the Huaguang Pavilion with guests, recited ci verses from a dream, asked for water to drink, and when it was brought smiled at the cup and died.

sentences.zh: 先自作挽詞，其語哀甚，讀者悲傷之。

translations.literal: He had earlier composed his own elegy; its language was deeply mournful, and readers were grieved.
translations.idiomatic: He had already written his own elegy; its language was so mournful that readers were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 年五十三，有文集四十卷。

translations.literal: He was fifty-three years old and left collected works in forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-three and left collected works in forty juan.

sentences.zh: 觀長於議論，文麗而思深。

translations.literal: Guan excelled at discourse; his writing was beautiful and his thought profound.
translations.idiomatic: Qin excelled at argument; his prose was elegant and his thought deep.

sentences.zh: 及死，軾聞之歎曰：「少游不幸死道路，哀哉！

translations.literal: When he died, Shi heard and sighed, "Shaoyou has unhappily died on the road — how pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of Qin's death, Su Shi sighed and said, "Shaoyou has died on the road — how pitiful!

sentences.zh: 世豈復有斯人乎！」

translations.literal: Will the world ever again have such a man!"
translations.idiomatic: Will the world ever see his like again!"

sentences.zh: 弟覿字少章，覯字少儀，皆能文。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Di, style name Shaozhang, and Gou, style name Shaoyi, were both able writers.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Di (Shaozhang) and Gou (Shaoyi) were both accomplished writers.

sentences.zh: 張耒，字文潛，楚州淮陰人。

translations.literal: Zhang Lei, style name Wenqian, was a native of Huaiyin in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lei, whose style name was Wenqian, came from Huaiyin in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼穎異，十三歲能為文，十七時作《函關賦》，已傳人口。

translations.literal: In childhood he was exceptionally clever; at thirteen he could write essays, and at seventeen when he composed the "Fu on Hangu Pass" it was already on people's lips.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was exceptionally bright; at thirteen he could write essays, and at seventeen his "Fu on Hangu Pass" was already on everyone's lips.

sentences.zh: 遊學于陳，學官蘇轍愛之，因得從軾遊，軾亦深知之，稱其文汪洋沖澹，有一倡三歎之聲。

translations.literal: He studied in Chen, where the academic officer Su Zhe favored him and thus he was able to follow Shi. Shi also knew him deeply and praised his writing as vast and tranquil, with the resonance of one voice and three sighs.
translations.idiomatic: He studied in Chen, where academic officer Su Zhe took a liking to him and introduced him to Su Shi. Su Shi came to know him well and praised his writing as vast and serene, with the resonance of a single voice drawing sighs from all who heard.

sentences.zh: 弱冠第進士，曆臨淮主簿、壽安尉、咸平縣丞。

translations.literal: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and successively served as registrar of Linhuai, sheriff of Shou'an, and assistant magistrate of Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and served in turn as registrar in Linhuai, sheriff in Shou'an, and assistant magistrate in Xianping.

sentences.zh: 入為太學錄，範純仁以館閣薦試，遷秘書省正字、著作佐郎、秘書丞、著作郎、史館檢討。

translations.literal: He entered service as recorder of the Imperial University. Fan Chunren recommended him for the palace archives examination; he was transferred to rectifier of texts in the Secretariat, assistant compiler, secretary of the Palace Library, compiler, and reviser of the History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as recorder of the Imperial University. Fan Chunren recommended him for the palace archives examination, after which he rose through the posts of rectifier of texts, assistant compiler, secretary of the Palace Library, compiler, and History Academy reviser.

sentences.zh: 居三館八年，顧義自守，泊如也。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the Three Academies for eight years, mindful of righteousness and self-restraint, tranquil as ever.
translations.idiomatic: He spent eight years in the Three Academies, mindful of duty and self-restraint, as tranquil as ever.

sentences.zh: 擢起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to attendant in the Office for Recording the Emperor's Actions.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant in the Office for Recording the Emperor's Actions.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，請郡，以直龍圖閣知潤州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era he requested a prefecture and was made prefect of Runzhou with the designation Directly Attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaosheng reign he asked for a provincial post and was made prefect of Runzhou with the title Directly Attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 坐黨籍，徙宣州，謫監黃州酒稅，徙復州。

translations.literal: Because of the faction list he was moved to Xuanzhou, demoted to supervise the wine tax of Huangzhou, then transferred to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Listed among the faction, he was moved to Xuanzhou, demoted to supervising the wine tax in Huangzhou, then transferred to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，起為通判黃州，知兗州，召為太常少卿，甫數月，復出知潁州、汝州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne he was recalled as vice-prefect of Huangzhou and prefect of Yanzhou, summoned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but after only a few months was again sent out as prefect of Yingzhou and Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong took the throne he was recalled as vice-prefect of Huangzhou and prefect of Yanzhou, then summoned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; after only a few months he was sent out again as prefect of Yingzhou and Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇甯初，復坐黨籍落職，主管明道宮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongning era he again suffered removal from office because of the faction list and was put in charge of the Mingdao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongning reign he was again struck from office on the faction list and placed in charge of the Mingdao Palace.

sentences.zh: 初，耒在潁，聞蘇軾訃，為舉哀行服，言者以為言，遂貶房州別駕，安置于黃。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Lei was in Ying, he heard of Shi's death and performed mourning rites and wore mourning garments. Critics impeached him for this and he was demoted to vice-prefect of Fangzhou and settled at Huang.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Yingzhou he heard of Su Shi's death and went into mourning dress. Critics denounced this as improper, and he was demoted to vice-prefect of Fangzhou and exiled to Huang.

sentences.zh: 五年，得自便，居陳州。

translations.literal: After five years he was granted freedom of movement and lived in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After five years he was allowed to move freely and settled in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 耒儀觀甚偉，有雄才，筆力絕健，于騷詞尤長。

translations.literal: Lei's bearing was imposing; he had heroic talent and an exceptionally vigorous brush, especially accomplished in sao-style verse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang had an imposing presence, bold talent, and an exceptionally powerful pen, especially in sao-style verse.

sentences.zh: 時二蘇及黃庭堅、晁補之輩相繼沒，耒獨存，士人就學者眾，分日載酒肴飲食之。

translations.literal: At the time the two Sus, Huang Tingjian, Chao Buzhi, and their circle had died one after another; Lei alone remained. Scholars who came to study were many, and on appointed days they brought wine and food to share.
translations.idiomatic: By then the two Sus, Huang Tingjian, Chao Buzhi, and their circle had all passed away; Zhang alone remained. Scholars flocked to study with him, taking turns to bring wine and food on appointed days.

sentences.zh: 誨人作文以理為主，嘗著論云：「自《六經》以下，至於諸子百氏騷人辯士論述，大抵皆將以為寓理之具也。

translations.literal: He taught others to write with principle as the master, and once wrote in an essay: "From the Six Classics down to the discourses of the hundred schools, sao poets, and debaters, all are broadly to be taken as instruments for lodging principle.
translations.idiomatic: He taught that writing should be grounded in principle, and once argued in an essay: "From the Six Classics down through the hundred schools, sao poets, and debaters, nearly all writing is ultimately a vehicle for embodying principle.

sentences.zh: 故學文之端，急於明理，如知文而不務理，求文之工，世未嘗有也。

translations.literal: Therefore the beginning of learning writing urgently lies in clarifying principle; if one knows writing but does not pursue principle, to seek literary mastery — the world has never seen it.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the first step in learning to write is to grasp principle; anyone who pursues literary skill without grounding it in principle has never truly mastered the art.

sentences.zh: 夫決水于江、河、淮、海也，順道而行，滔滔汨汨，日夜不止，沖砥柱，絕呂梁，放於江湖而納之海，其舒為淪漣，鼓為波濤，激之為風飆，怒之為雷霆，蛟龍魚鱉，噴薄出沒，是水之奇變也。

translations.literal: When water is channeled into the Yangzi, Yellow River, Huai, and sea, it follows the Way and flows on, surging and rushing day and night without cease, striking the Pillar Rock, passing Mount Liang, released into lakes and rivers and received into the sea. At ease it becomes ripples; stirred it becomes waves; roused it becomes gales; angered it becomes thunder; dragons, fish, and turtles burst forth and vanish — these are the marvelous transformations of water.
translations.idiomatic: When water is directed into the great rivers and the sea, it follows its natural course—surging day and night without cease, striking the Pillar Rock, sweeping past Mount Liang, pouring into lakes and rivers and at last into the sea. At ease it spreads in ripples; stirred it rises in waves; quickened it becomes gales; enraged it becomes thunder; dragons, fish, and turtles burst forth and vanish—these are water's marvelous transformations.

sentences.zh: 水之初，豈若是哉！

translations.literal: In its beginning, was water ever like this!
translations.idiomatic: Water in its origin was never like this!

sentences.zh: 順道而決之，因其所遇而變生焉。

translations.literal: Following the Way it is channeled forth, and transformations arise according to what it encounters.
translations.idiomatic: Directed along its proper course, it takes on new forms according to whatever it meets.

sentences.zh: 溝瀆東決而西竭，下滿而上虛，日夜激之，欲見其奇，彼其所至者，蛙蛭之玩耳。

translations.literal: When ditches burst eastward and run dry in the west, full below and empty above, stirred day and night to display marvels — what they reach is merely sport for frogs and leeches.
translations.idiomatic: When ditches burst eastward and run dry in the west, brimming below and hollow above, stirred day and night to force marvels—what they amount to is play for frogs and leeches.

sentences.zh: 江、河、淮、海之水，理達之文也，不求奇而奇至矣。

translations.literal: The waters of the Yangzi, Yellow River, Huai, and sea are writing in which principle is attained; without seeking strangeness, strangeness arrives.
translations.idiomatic: The waters of the great rivers and sea are writing in which principle is fully realized; without chasing novelty, marvel appears of itself.

sentences.zh: 激溝瀆而求水之奇，此無見於理，而欲以言語句讀為奇，反覆咀嚼，卒亦無有，文之陋也。」

translations.literal: To stir ditches seeking the marvels of water shows no insight into principle; to seek strangeness in phrasing and punctuation, chewing over and over, in the end there is nothing — the baseness of writing."
translations.idiomatic: To churn ditches in search of water's marvels shows no grasp of principle; to chase strangeness in phrasing and punctuation, chewing phrases over and over until nothing remains—that is the poverty of bad writing."

sentences.zh: 學者以為至言。

translations.literal: Scholars regarded this as ultimate doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars took this as the last word on the subject.

sentences.zh: 作詩晚歲益務平淡，效白居易體，而樂府效張籍。

translations.literal: In composing poetry, in his later years he increasingly pursued plainness, imitating Bai Juyi's style, while his yuefu imitated Zhang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he increasingly sought plainness in poetry, following Bai Juyi's manner, while his yuefu ballads followed Zhang Ji.

sentences.zh: 久於投閑，家益貧，郡守翟汝文欲為買公田，謝不取。

translations.literal: Long cast into idleness, his family grew poorer. The prefect Zhai Ruwen wished to buy public fields for him, but he declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: After long years out of office his family grew poorer still. Prefect Zhai Ruwen offered to buy him public farmland, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 晚監南嶽廟，主管崇福宮，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In his later years he supervised the Southern Marchmount Temple and was put in charge of the Chongfu Palace; he died at sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he oversaw the Southern Marchmount Temple and the Chongfu Palace; he died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，贈集英殿修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan era he was posthumously given the title Compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan reign he was posthumously made Compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence.

sentences.zh: 陳師道

translations.literal: Chen Shidao
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shidao

sentences.zh: 陳師道，字履常，一字無己，彭城人。

translations.literal: Chen Shidao, courtesy name Lüchang, also styled Wuji, a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shidao, courtesy name Lüchang, also known as Wuji, was a native of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 少而好學苦志，年十六，摎以文謁曾鞏，鞏一見奇之，許其以文著，時人未之知也，留受業。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and pursued it with bitter resolve. At sixteen he took his writings to visit Zeng Gong; Zeng was struck with wonder at first sight, assured him he would distinguish himself by writing though the world did not yet know him, and kept him to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved learning and pursued it with fierce resolve. At sixteen he brought his writings to Zeng Gong; Zeng was astonished at first sight, assured him he would make his name through letters though the world had not yet heard of him, and kept him on as a student.

sentences.zh: 熙甯中，王氏經學盛行，師道心非其說，遂絕意進取。

translations.literal: During the Xining era Wang's classical learning prevailed; Shidao's heart rejected its doctrines and he utterly gave up thoughts of advancement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era the Wang clan's classical learning held sway; Shidao inwardly rejected its teachings and completely abandoned any thought of official advancement.

sentences.zh: 鞏典五朝史事，得自擇其屬，朝廷以白衣難之。

translations.literal: Gong was in charge of the histories of five dynasties and could choose his own assistants; the court found it awkward because he was a commoner in plain robes.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gong was compiling the histories of five dynasties and could choose his own assistants; the court balked at appointing a man who was still a commoner in plain robes.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，蘇軾、傅堯俞、孫覺薦其文行，起為徐州教援，又用梁燾薦，為太學博士。

translations.literal: Early in the Yuanyou era Su Shi, Fu Yaoyu, and Sun Jue recommended his conduct and writing; he was raised to Instructor at Xuzhou, and on Liang Tao's recommendation again became Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era Su Shi, Fu Yaoyu, and Sun Jue recommended his character and writing; he was appointed Instructor at Xuzhou, and on Liang Tao's recommendation was made Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 言者謂在官嘗越境出南京見軾，改教授潁州。

translations.literal: Critics said that while in office he had once crossed the border to leave Nanjing to see Su Shi; he was transferred to Instructor at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that while in office he had once crossed jurisdictional lines to leave Nanjing and visit Su Shi; he was reassigned as Instructor at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又論其進非科第，罷歸。

translations.literal: They also argued that his advancement had not been through the examination route, and he was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: They also argued that his promotion had not come through the examination track, and he was dismissed to return home.

sentences.zh: 調彭澤令，不赴。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Pengze but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Pengze but declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 家素貧，或經日不炊，妻子慍見，弗恤也。

translations.literal: His family had always been poor; sometimes for days no meal was cooked. His wife and children showed resentment when they saw him, but he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: His family had always been poor; sometimes days would pass without a fire lit for cooking. His wife and children showed their anger plainly, but he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為秘書省正字，卒，年四十九，友人鄒浩買棺斂之。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned as Corrector in the Secretariat; he died at forty-nine. His friend Zou Hao bought a coffin and laid him out.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was summoned as Corrector in the Secretariat; he died at forty-nine. His friend Zou Hao bought a coffin and laid him to rest.

sentences.zh: 師道高介有節，安貧樂道。

translations.literal: Shidao was lofty and principled, content in poverty and devoted to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was lofty in character and firm in principle, content in poverty and devoted to the Way.

sentences.zh: 于諸經尤邃《詩》、《禮》，為文精深雅奧。

translations.literal: Among the classics he was especially deep in the Odes and the Rites; his prose was profound, refined, and abstruse.
translations.idiomatic: Among the classics he was especially profound in the Odes and the Rites; his prose was deep, refined, and recondite.

sentences.zh: 喜作詩，自雲學黃庭堅，至其高處，或謂過之，然小不中意，輒焚去，今存者才十一。

translations.literal: He delighted in composing poetry, saying himself that he studied Huang Tingjian; at his heights some said he surpassed him, yet whatever fell even slightly short of his intent he would burn—of what survives today barely a tenth remains.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in writing poetry and said himself that he studied Huang Tingjian; at his best some held he surpassed him, yet anything that fell even slightly short of his standard he burned—of what survives today barely one part in ten.

sentences.zh: 世徒喜誦其詩文，至若奧學至行，或莫之聞也。

translations.literal: The world merely delights in reciting his poetry and prose; as for his recondite learning and supreme conduct, some never heard of them at all.
translations.idiomatic: The world merely delights in reciting his poems and essays; as for his deepest learning and highest conduct, many never heard of them at all.

sentences.zh: 嘗銘黃樓，曾子固謂如秦石。

translations.literal: He once inscribed the Yellow Tower; Zeng Zigu said it was like Qin stone.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote an inscription for the Yellow Tower; Zeng Gong said it was like stone from Qin.

sentences.zh: 初，游京師逾年，未嘗一至貴人之門，傅堯俞欲識之，先以問秦觀，觀曰：「是人非持刺字、俯顏色、伺候乎公卿之門者，殆難至也。」

translations.literal: At first, traveling in the capital for over a year, he never once set foot at a powerful man's door. Fu Yaoyu wished to make his acquaintance and first asked Qin Guan, who said: "This is not one who carries calling cards, bows his face, and waits upon grandees' doors—he will be hard to reach."
translations.idiomatic: When he first traveled to the capital he stayed more than a year without once setting foot inside a powerful man's door. Fu Yaoyu wished to know him and first asked Qin Guan, who said, "This is not the sort who carries calling cards, bows his face, and waits on grandees at their gates—he will be hard to reach."

sentences.zh: 堯俞曰：「非所望也，吾將見之，懼其不吾見也，子能介於陳君乎？」

translations.literal: Fu Yaoyu said: "That is not what I hope for. I shall go see him myself, fearing he will not receive me. Can you introduce me to Master Chen?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yaoyu said, "That is not what I have in mind. I mean to go see him myself, for I fear he will not receive me. Can you introduce me to Master Chen?"

sentences.zh: 知其貧，懷金欲為饋，比至，聽其論議，益敬畏，不敢出。

translations.literal: Knowing he was poor, he carried gold intending it as a gift; when he arrived and heard his discourse, he grew only more in awe and respect and did not dare bring it out.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing how poor he was, Fu carried gold intending it as a gift; but when he arrived and heard him discourse, he grew only more awed and respectful and did not dare produce it.

sentences.zh: 章惇在樞府，將薦於朝，亦屬觀延致。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun was at the Bureau of Military Affairs and was about to recommend him to court; he also entrusted Qin Guan to extend an invitation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun was at the Bureau of Military Affairs and was about to recommend him to the court; he also asked Qin Guan to convey an invitation.

sentences.zh: 師道答曰：「辱書，諭以章公降屈年德，以禮見招，不佞何以得此，豈侯嘗欺之耶？

translations.literal: Shidao replied: "I am honored by your letter, informing me that Lord Zhang humbles his years and dignity and summons me with courtesy—how could one so unworthy merit this? Surely you have never deceived me?
translations.idiomatic: Shidao replied, "I am honored by your letter, which tells me that Lord Zhang humbles his years and standing and summons me with courtesy—how could one so unworthy deserve this? Surely you have never misled me?

sentences.zh: 公卿不下士，尚矣，乃特見於今而親於其身，幸孰大焉。

translations.literal: That grandees do not descend to scholars is an old principle; yet now he specially receives me in person—what fortune could be greater?
translations.idiomatic: That grandees do not descend to scholars is an ancient rule; yet now he receives me in person—what fortune could be greater?

sentences.zh: 愚雖不足以齒士，猶當從侯之後，順下風以成公之名。

translations.literal: Though I am too unworthy to rank among scholars, I ought still to follow in your lordship's train, bowing to the lower wind to complete your lordship's fame.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am scarcely fit to rank among scholars, I ought still to follow in your lordship's train and bow to the lower wind to complete your lordship's renown.

sentences.zh: 然先王之制，士不傳贄為臣，則不見於王公，所以成禮而其敝必至自鬻，故先王謹其始以為之防，而為士者世守焉。

translations.literal: Yet the ancient kings' institution: if a scholar does not pass his tribute token to become a minister, he does not appear before kings and dukes—this completes the rites, and its abuse inevitably leads to selling oneself; therefore the ancient kings were strict at the beginning to set a defense, and scholars through the ages have guarded it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ancient kings ordained that unless a scholar presents his tribute token to become a minister, he does not appear before kings and dukes—this completes the ritual, and its abuse inevitably leads to selling oneself; therefore the ancient kings were strict at the outset to guard against it, and scholars through the ages have upheld it.

sentences.zh: 師道於公，前有貴賤之嫌，後無平生之舊，公雖可見，禮可去乎？

translations.literal: Between Shidao and your lordship, before there is the suspicion of noble and base; behind, no lifelong acquaintance—the lord may be seen, but can the rites be set aside?
translations.idiomatic: Between Shidao and your lordship, beforehand there is the taint of noble and base, and afterward no lifelong bond—the lord may be seen, but can the rites be cast aside?

sentences.zh: 且公之見招，蓋以能守區區之禮也，若昧冒法義，聞命走門，則失其所以見招，公又何取焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, your lordship's summons is surely because I can guard this petty ritual; if I blindly violate law and right, hear the command and run to your door, then I lose the reason I was summoned—what would your lordship find in that?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your lordship summons me surely because I can uphold this humble ritual; if I blindly violate law and duty, hear the command and run to your door, then I forfeit the very reason I was summoned—what would your lordship gain from that?

sentences.zh: 雖然，有一於此，幸公之他日成功謝事，幅巾東歸，師道當禦款段，乘下澤，候公於東門外，尚未晚也。」

translations.literal: Nevertheless, on one point: should your lordship one day succeed, retire from office, and return east in plain headcloth, Shidao will drive a piebald nag and ride a low cart to await your lordship outside the eastern gate—not yet too late."
translations.idiomatic: Still, on one point: should your lordship one day succeed, retire from office, and return east in plain headcloth, Shidao will drive a piebald pony and ride a low swamp-cart to await your lordship outside the eastern gate—and that will not yet be too late."

sentences.zh: 及惇為相，又致意焉，終不往。

translations.literal: When Dun became chief councilor he again conveyed his intent; in the end Shidao never went.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun became chief councilor he again sent his regards; in the end Shidao never went.

sentences.zh: 官潁時，蘇軾知州事，待之絕席，欲參諸門弟子間，而師道賦詩有「向來一瓣香，敬為曾南豐」之語，其自守如是。

translations.literal: When he held office at Ying, Su Shi managed prefectural affairs and treated him with utmost honor, wishing to have him join the ranks of disciples at his gate; yet Shidao's poem had the lines "All along one stick of incense, offered in reverence to Zeng Nanfeng"—such was his self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: While he served at Ying, Su Shi managed prefectural affairs and treated him with the highest honor, wishing to have him counted among the disciples at his gate; yet Shidao wrote in a poem, "All along one stick of incense, offered in reverence to Zeng Nanfeng"—such was how he held himself.

sentences.zh: 與趙挺之友婿，素惡其人，適預郊祀行禮，寒甚，衣無綿，妻就假于挺之家，問所從得，卻去，不肯服，遂以寒疾死。

translations.literal: He was son-in-law to a friend of Zhao Tingzhi, whom he had always detested. On one occasion he was taking part in suburban sacrifice rites in extreme cold, his clothes without cotton padding; his wife borrowed from Tingzhi's household, asked where they came from, then returned them and refused to wear them; he consequently died of cold sickness.
translations.idiomatic: He was son-in-law to a friend of Zhao Tingzhi, a man he had always detested. Once, while taking part in suburban sacrifice rites in bitter cold, his clothes had no cotton padding; his wife borrowed garments from Tingzhi's household, and when she learned where they came from she returned them and refused to wear them; he consequently died of a cold-induced illness.

sentences.zh: 李廌，字方叔，其先自鄆徙華。

translations.literal: Li Zhi, courtesy name Fangshu; his ancestors moved from Yun to Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi, courtesy name Fangshu, was descended from a family that had moved from Yun to Hua.

sentences.zh: 廌六歲而孤，能自奮立，少長，以學問稱鄉里。

translations.literal: Zhi was orphaned at six but could struggle to stand on his own; growing up he was famed in his district for learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was orphaned at six yet could rouse himself to stand on his own; as he grew he won renown in his district for learning.

sentences.zh: 謁蘇軾于黃州，贄文求知。

translations.literal: He visited Su Shi at Huangzhou and presented a writing requesting to be known.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Su Shi at Huangzhou and presented a composition asking to be taken as a student.

sentences.zh: 軾謂其筆墨瀾翻，有飛沙走石之勢，拊其背曰：「子之才，萬人敵也，抗之以高節，莫之能禦矣。」

translations.literal: Su said his brushwork surged like flying sand and rushing stones, and patting his back said: "Your talent is a match for ten thousand men; set against it lofty integrity and none can overcome you."
translations.idiomatic: Su said his brush surged like flying sand and rushing stone, and patting his back said, "Your talent is a match for ten thousand men; set it against lofty integrity and none can overcome you."

sentences.zh: 廌再拜受教。

translations.literal: Zhi bowed again to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi bowed again to receive the teaching.

sentences.zh: 而家素貧，三世未葬，一夕，撫枕流涕曰：「吾忠孝焉是學，而親未葬，何以學為！」

translations.literal: Yet his family had always been poor—three generations unburied. One night he stroked his pillow and wept, saying: "What I study is loyalty and filial piety, yet my kin lie unburied—what use is study!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet his family had always been poor—three generations lay unburied. One night he stroked his pillow and wept, saying, "What I study is loyalty and filial piety, yet my kin lie unburied—what use is study!"

sentences.zh: 旦而別軾，將客游四方，以蕆其事。

translations.literal: At dawn he bade farewell to Su, and would travel the four quarters as a guest to raise funds for the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he took leave of Su and set out to travel the realm as a guest, seeking to raise funds for the burials.

sentences.zh: 軾解衣為助，又作詩以勸風義者。

translations.literal: Su took off his robe to help and also composed a poem to urge men of moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: Su took off his own robe to help and also wrote a poem urging men of principle to assist.

sentences.zh: 於是不數年，盡致累世之喪三十餘柩，歸窆華山下，範鎮為表墓以美之。

translations.literal: Within not many years he had gathered over thirty coffins of accumulated generations' dead and buried them at the foot of Mount Hua; Fan Zhen wrote a tomb inscription to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he had gathered more than thirty coffins of the dead accumulated over generations and buried them at the foot of Mount Hua; Fan Zhen wrote a tomb inscription to praise him.

sentences.zh: 益閉門讀書，又數年，再見軾，軾閱其所著，歎曰：「張耒、秦觀之流也。」

translations.literal: He shut his doors to read books all the more; after several years he saw Su again; Su read what he had written and sighed: "Of Zhang Lei and Qin Guan's kind."
translations.idiomatic: He shut his doors and read all the more diligently; after several years he saw Su again; Su read what he had written and sighed, "Of Zhang Lei and Qin Guan's company."

sentences.zh: 鄉舉試禮部，軾典貢舉，遺之，賦詩以自責。

translations.literal: Nominated by his district he tried at the Ministry of Rites; Su presided over the examinations and omitted him, composing a poem to reproach himself.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated by his district he entered the Ministry of Rites examination; Su presided over the examinations and passed him over, writing a poem to reproach himself.

sentences.zh: 呂大防歎曰：「有司試藝，乃失此奇才耶！」

translations.literal: Lü Dafang sighed and said: "The authorities tested arts—yet missed this extraordinary talent!"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dafang sighed and said, "The examiners tested literary skill—yet missed this extraordinary talent!"

sentences.zh: 軾與范祖禹謀曰：「廌雖在山林，其文有錦衣玉食氣，棄奇寶于路隅，昔人所歎，我曹得無意哉！」

translations.literal: Su and Fan Zuyu took counsel: "Though Zhi is in mountains and woods, his writing has the air of brocade robes and jade food—to cast a wondrous treasure by the roadside, as ancients lamented—can we be without scruple?"
translations.idiomatic: Su and Fan Zuyu took counsel together: "Though Zhi dwells in mountains and woods, his writing has the air of brocade robes and jade fare—to cast a wondrous treasure by the roadside, as the ancients lamented—can we be without scruple?"

sentences.zh: 將同薦諸朝，未幾，相繼去國，不果。

translations.literal: They were about to recommend him together to court; before long they left office in succession and it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: They were about to recommend him jointly to the court; before long they left office one after another and it never came to pass.

sentences.zh: 軾亡，廌哭之慟，曰：「吾愧不能死知己，至於事師之勤，渠敢以生死為間！」

translations.literal: When Su died, Zhi wept in deepest grief and said: "I am ashamed I could not die for my knower; as for serving my teacher with diligence, how dare I let life and death stand between!"
translations.idiomatic: When Su died, Zhi wept in deepest grief and said, "I am ashamed I could not die for my knower; as for serving my teacher with full devotion, how dare I let life and death stand between us!"

sentences.zh: 即走許、汝間，相地卜兆授其子，作文祭之曰：「皇天后土，鑒一生忠義之心；

translations.literal: He straightaway went between Xu and Ru, chose ground and divined a site, entrusting it to Su's son; he wrote a memorial text saying: "Sovereign Heaven and Mother Earth, behold a lifetime's loyal and righteous heart;
translations.idiomatic: He straightaway went to the region between Xu and Ru, chose ground and divined a burial site, entrusting it to Su's son; he wrote a memorial text saying, "Sovereign Heaven and Mother Earth, behold a lifetime's heart of loyalty and righteousness;

sentences.zh: 名山大川，還萬古英靈之氣。」

translations.literal: mountains and great rivers, restore ten thousand ages' heroic spirit."
translations.idiomatic: mountains and great rivers, restore the heroic spirit of ten thousand ages."

sentences.zh: 詞語奇壯，讀者為悚。

translations.literal: The language was marvelous and vigorous; readers were struck with awe.
translations.idiomatic: The language was marvelous and forceful; readers were shaken with awe.

sentences.zh: 中年絕進取意，謂潁為人物淵藪，始定居長社，縣令李佐及裏人買宅處之。

translations.literal: In mid-life he utterly gave up thoughts of advancement, saying Ying was a deep pool of talented men; he first settled at Changshe, where Magistrate Li Zuo and neighbors bought a house to lodge him.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-life he utterly abandoned thoughts of advancement, saying that Ying was a deep reservoir of talented men; he first settled at Changshe, where Magistrate Li Zuo and local people bought a house to lodge him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 廌喜論古今治亂，條暢曲折，辯而中理。

translations.literal: Zhi delighted in discussing past and present order and chaos, items orderly and turns well set, argumentative yet hitting principle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi delighted in discussing order and chaos through the ages, laying out points in clear sequence with well-turned argument that yet struck the mark of reason.

sentences.zh: 當喧溷倉卒間如不經意，睥睨而起，落筆如飛馳。

translations.literal: Amid clamor and hurry, as if paying no mind, he would glance up and set brush to paper like flying.
translations.idiomatic: Amid clamor and haste he would seem to pay no mind, then glance up and set brush to paper as if flying.

sentences.zh: 元祐求言，上《忠諫書》、《忠厚論》並獻《兵鑒》二萬言論西事。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou call for counsel he submitted the "Book of Loyal Remonstrance," the "Treatise on Loyalty and Thickness," and also offered "Military Mirror"—twenty thousand characters on western affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou call for counsel he submitted the Book of Loyal Remonstrance and the Treatise on Loyalty and Thickness, and also presented Military Mirror—twenty thousand characters on western affairs.

sentences.zh: 朝廷擒羌酋鬼章，將致法，廌深論利害，以為殺之無益，願加寬大，當時韙其言。

translations.literal: When the court captured the Qiang chieftain Guizhang and was about to apply the law, Zhi argued deeply on benefit and harm, holding that killing him was no use and urging leniency; at the time they approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: When the court captured the Qiang chieftain Guizhang and was about to punish him by law, Zhi argued at length on benefit and harm, holding that executing him would serve no purpose and urging clemency; at the time the court approved his view.

sentences.zh: 劉恕，字道原，筠州人。

translations.literal: Liu Shu, courtesy name Daoyuan, a native of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu, courtesy name Daoyuan, was a native of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 父渙字凝之，為潁上令，以剛直不能事上官，棄去。

translations.literal: His father Huan, courtesy name Ningzhi, was magistrate of Yingshang; because of upright rigidity he could not serve superiors and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Huan, courtesy name Ningzhi, served as magistrate of Yingshang; because of his upright rigidity he could not accommodate his superiors and resigned.

sentences.zh: 家于廬山之陽，時年五十。

translations.literal: The family settled on the southern slope of Mount Lu when he was fifty.
translations.idiomatic: The family settled on the southern slope of Mount Lu when Huan was fifty.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修與渙，同年進士也，高其節，作《廬山高》詩以美之。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu and Huan had been fellow graduates the same year; he esteemed his integrity and wrote "Mount Lu High" to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu and Huan had passed the examinations in the same year; Xiu esteemed his integrity and wrote Mount Lu High to praise him.

sentences.zh: 渙居廬山三十餘年，環堵蕭然，饘粥以為食，而遊心塵垢之外，超然無戚戚意，以壽終。

translations.literal: Huan dwelt on Mount Lu over thirty years, one bare room desolate, gruel his food, yet his mind roamed beyond dust and defilement, utterly without anxious care, and he died at a ripe old age.
translations.idiomatic: Huan lived on Mount Lu for more than thirty years in a single bare room, gruel his only food, yet his mind roamed beyond the dust of the world, utterly free of anxious care, and he died at a ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 恕少穎悟，書過目即成誦。

translations.literal: Shu from youth was sharp and perceptive; a book once seen he could recite.
translations.idiomatic: Shu from youth was quick and perceptive; whatever book he saw once he could recite.

sentences.zh: 八歲時，坐客有言孔子無兄弟者，恕應聲曰：「以其兄之子妻之。」

translations.literal: When he was eight, a guest remarked that Confucius had no brothers; Shu answered on the spot: "He gave his brother's daughter in marriage."
translations.idiomatic: When he was eight, a guest remarked that Confucius had no brothers; Shu answered on the spot, "He gave his brother's daughter in marriage."

sentences.zh: 一坐驚異。

translations.literal: The whole company were startled.
translations.idiomatic: The whole company were astonished.

sentences.zh: 年十三，欲應制科，從人假《漢》、《唐書》，閱月皆歸之。

translations.literal: At thirteen he wished to enter the decree examination; borrowing the Han and Tang histories, in a month he returned them.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he wished to enter the Decree examination; borrowing the Han and Tang histories, within a month he had returned them.

sentences.zh: 謁丞相晏殊，問以事，反覆詰難，殊不能對。

translations.literal: He visited Chief Councillor Yan Shu and was questioned on affairs; back and forth they pressed and challenged until Yan could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Chief Councillor Yan Shu and was questioned on affairs; back and forth they pressed and challenged him until Yan could not answer.

sentences.zh: 恕在钜鹿時，召至府，重禮之，使講《春秋》，殊親帥官屬往聽。

translations.literal: When Shu was at Julu he was summoned to the prefectural office, treated with heavy honor, and made to lecture on the Spring and Autumn; Yan himself led officials to hear.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was at Julu he was summoned to the prefectural office, treated with the greatest respect, and made to lecture on the Spring and Autumn Annals; Yan himself led the officials to listen.

sentences.zh: 未冠，舉進士，時有詔，能講經義者別奏名，應詔者才數十人，恕以《春秋》、《禮記》對，先列注疏，次引先儒異說，末乃斷以己意，凡二十問，所對皆然，主司異之，擢為第一。

translations.literal: Before his capping he passed the metropolitan examination; there was then an edict that those able to expound canonical meaning might be separately memorialized. Those who responded numbered only several tens; Shu answered on the Spring and Autumn and the Record of Rites, first citing commentaries, then citing earlier masters' differing views, finally judging with his own opinion—for twenty questions his answers were all thus. The examiners marveled and ranked him first.
translations.idiomatic: Before his capping ceremony he passed the metropolitan examination; an edict then allowed those able to expound canonical meaning to be separately memorialized. Only several dozen candidates responded; Shu answered on the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Record of Rites, first citing the commentaries, then citing differing views of earlier masters, and finally judging with his own opinion—for twenty questions his answers were all of this kind. The examiners marveled and ranked him first.

sentences.zh: 他文亦入高等，而廷試不中格，更下國子試講經，復第一，遂賜第。

translations.literal: His other compositions also entered the upper grade, but the palace examination did not pass the standard; he was sent down to the Directorate to try again on classics exposition, again first, and was then granted degree.
translations.idiomatic: His other compositions also placed in the upper grade, but the palace examination did not meet the standard; he was sent down to the Directorate to try again on classics exposition, again placed first, and was then granted his degree.

sentences.zh: 調钜鹿主簿、和川令，發強擿伏，一時能吏自以為不及。

translations.literal: Posted as Registrar at Julu and Magistrate of Hechuan, exposing the powerful and ferreting out the hidden—for a time capable clerks thought themselves his inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as registrar at Julu and magistrate of Hechuan, he exposed the powerful and ferreted out what was hidden—for a time even the most capable officials considered themselves his inferior.

sentences.zh: 恕為人重意義，急然諾。

translations.literal: Shu as a man set weight on righteousness and was swift to keep promises.
translations.idiomatic: As a man Shu set great weight on righteousness and was swift to keep his word.

sentences.zh: 郡守得罪被劾，屬吏皆連坐下獄，恕獨恤其妻子，如己骨肉，又面數轉運使深文峻詆。

translations.literal: A prefect having offended was impeached; subordinate officials were all implicated and thrown into prison. Shu alone comforted wife and children as his own flesh, and moreover openly reproached the transport commissioner for harsh phrases and severe slander.
translations.idiomatic: When a prefect had offended and was impeached, his subordinate officials were all implicated and thrown into prison; Shu alone comforted the man's wife and children as if they were his own flesh, and moreover openly reproached the transport commissioner for twisting the law with harsh words.

sentences.zh: 篤好史學，自太史公所記，下至周顯德末，紀傳之外至私記雜說，無所不覽，上下數千載間，钜微之事，如指諸掌。

translations.literal: He devoted himself warmly to historical studies—from what Grand Historian Sima Qian recorded down to the end of Zhou Xiande, annals and biographies besides down to private records and miscellaneous tales, nothing he did not read. Across several thousand years, great and minute matters were as if laid on his palm.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself passionately to historical studies—from what Grand Historian Sima Qian recorded down to the end of the Xiande reign of Later Zhou, and beyond annals and biographies to private records and miscellaneous tales, there was nothing he did not read. Across several thousand years, matters great and small lay on his palm as if in plain sight.

sentences.zh: 司馬光編次《資治通鑒》，英宗命自擇館閣英才共修之。

translations.literal: Sima Guang was compiling the Comprehensive Mirror; Emperor Yingzong ordered him to choose talented men of the palace to compile together.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang was compiling the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government; Emperor Yingzong ordered him to choose talented men from the palace institutes to compile it jointly.

sentences.zh: 光對曰：「館閣文學之士誠多，至於專精史學，臣得而知者，唯劉恕耳。

translations.literal: Guang replied: "Men of letters in the palace are indeed many; as for those who specialize in history, of whom your servant is aware, only Liu Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Guang replied, "Men of letters in the palace are indeed numerous; but as for those who specialize in history, of whom your servant is aware, there is only Liu Shu.

sentences.zh: 即召為局僚，遇史事紛錯難治者，輒以諉恕。

translations.literal: He was at once summoned as a bureau assistant; whenever historical matters were tangled and hard to settle they were assigned to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once summoned as a bureau assistant; whenever historical matters were tangled and hard to resolve, they were turned over to Shu.

sentences.zh: 恕于魏、晉以後事，考證差繆，最為精詳。

translations.literal: For events after Wei and Jin, examining texts and correcting errors, he was most precise and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: For events after Wei and Jin, in examining texts and correcting errors, he was the most precise and detailed.

sentences.zh: 王安石與之有舊，欲引置三司條例。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi was old friends with him and wished to appoint him to the Fiscal and Commercial Regulations Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was an old friend and wished to appoint him to the Fiscal and Commercial Regulations Commission.

sentences.zh: 恕以不習金穀為辭，因言天子方屬公大政，宜恢張堯、舜之道以佐明主，不應以利為先。

translations.literal: Shu declined on grounds of not being versed in revenue and grain, and said the Son of Heaven now entrusts your lordship with great affairs; you ought to extend the way of Yao and Shun to assist the enlightened sovereign—not take profit as the priority.
translations.idiomatic: Shu declined on the ground that he was not versed in revenue and grain accounts, and said, "The Son of Heaven now entrusts your lordship with great affairs; you ought to extend the way of Yao and Shun to assist the enlightened sovereign—not make profit the foremost concern."

sentences.zh: 又條陳所更法令不合眾心者，勸使復舊，至面刺其過，安石怒，變色如鐵，恕不少屈。

translations.literal: He also itemized statutes revised that did not accord with the people's hearts and urged restoration of the old; even to his face he pointed out faults. Anshi was angry, his face changing like iron; Shu did not bend slightly.
translations.idiomatic: He also itemized revised statutes that did not accord with the people's hearts and urged that the old laws be restored; he even pointed out Anshi's faults to his face. Anshi was furious, his expression turning iron-hard; Shu did not yield in the slightest.

sentences.zh: 或稠人廣坐，抗言其失無所避，遂與之絕。

translations.literal: Sometimes in crowded halls he spoke against his errors without avoidance; they broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes in crowded halls he spoke against Anshi's errors without the least avoidance; the two broke off relations entirely.

sentences.zh: 方安石用事，呼吸成禍福，高論之士，始異而終附之，面譽而背毀之，口順而心非之者，皆是也。

translations.literal: When Anshi held power, a breath could bring fortune or disaster; lofty debaters at first differed but in the end attached to him—praising to the face yet slandering behind, speaking agreeably yet dissenting in heart—such men were everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi held power, a single breath could bring fortune or disaster; lofty debaters who at first stood apart in the end attached themselves to him—praising to his face yet slandering behind it, speaking agreeably yet dissenting in their hearts—such men were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 恕奮厲不顧，直指其事，得失無所隱。

translations.literal: Shu roused himself without looking back, pointing straight at the matters, gain and loss concealed from none.
translations.idiomatic: Shu roused himself without looking back, pointing straight at the facts, concealing neither gain nor loss.

sentences.zh: 光出知永興軍，恕亦以親老，求監南康軍酒以就養，許即官修書。

translations.literal: When Guang went out as prefect of Yongxing Army, Shu too, his parents being elderly, requested supervision of Nan Kang Military Wine duties to support them; he was permitted to take office while continuing to compile the book.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang went out to serve as prefect of Yongxing, Shu too—his parents being elderly—requested appointment as supervisor of the Nan Kang military wine tax so he could support them nearby; he was permitted to take office while continuing to compile the book.

sentences.zh: 光判西京御史台，恕請詣光，留數月而歸。

translations.literal: Guang judged the Western Capital Censorate; Shu asked to visit Guang and stayed several months before returning.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang served as judge of the Western Capital Censorate, Shu asked to visit him and stayed several months before returning.

sentences.zh: 道得風攣疾，右手足廢，然苦學如故，少間，輒修書，病亟乃止。

translations.literal: On the road he contracted wind spasms; his right hand and foot were disabled, yet he studied bitterly as before—at every brief interval he would resume the book, stopping only when the illness grew critical.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he contracted wind spasms; his right hand and foot were crippled, yet he studied as bitterly as before—at every brief respite he would resume work on the book, stopping only when the illness grew critical.

sentences.zh: 官至秘書丞，卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: He reached office as Secretariat Assistant and died at forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Secretariat Assistant and died at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 恕為學，自歷數、地裏、官職、族姓至前代公府案牘，皆取以審證。

translations.literal: In scholarship, from calendrics, geography, offices, and clan names down to former dynasties' archival documents of government offices, he took all to examine and verify.
translations.idiomatic: In his scholarship, from calendrics, geography, offices, and clan names down to the archival documents of former dynasties' government bureaus, he took everything as material for examination and verification.

sentences.zh: 求書不遠數百里，身就之讀且抄，殆忘寢食。

translations.literal: Seeking books he would go several hundred li in person to read and copy, nearly forgetting sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: In search of books he would travel several hundred li in person to read and copy them, nearly forgetting sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 偕司馬光游萬安山，道旁有碑，讀之，乃五代列將，人所不知名者，恕能言其行事始終，歸驗舊史，信然。

translations.literal: Once traveling Mount Wan'an with Sima Guang, beside the road was a stele; reading it, it was a general of the Five Dynasties whose name men did not know. Shu could relate his career from start to finish; returning to check old histories, it proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Once, traveling Mount Wan'an with Sima Guang, they came upon a stele by the roadside; reading it, they found it commemorated a general of the Five Dynasties whose name no one knew. Shu could recount his career from beginning to end; when they returned and checked against old histories, it proved true.

sentences.zh: 宋次道知亳州，家多書，恕枉道借覽。

translations.literal: Song Cidao was magistrate of Bozhou; his household had many books. Shu went out of his way to borrow and read them.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Cidao served as magistrate of Bozhou, his household held a great library. Shu made a detour to borrow books and read through them.

sentences.zh: 次道日具饌為主人禮，恕曰：「此非吾所為來也，殊廢吾事。」

translations.literal: Cidao daily set out feasts as a host's courtesy. Shu said: "This is not what I came for—it greatly wastes my affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Cidao daily prepared feasts in the manner of a host. Shu said, "This is not why I came—it greatly wastes my work."

sentences.zh: 悉去之。

translations.literal: He had them all removed.
translations.idiomatic: He had them all removed.

sentences.zh: 獨閉閣，晝夜口誦手抄，留旬日，盡其書而去，目為之翳。

translations.literal: Alone he shut the pavilion, day and night reciting aloud and copying by hand; he stayed ten days, exhausted all the books and left—his eyes were clouded.
translations.idiomatic: He shut himself alone in the library pavilion, reciting aloud and copying by hand day and night. He stayed ten days, read through the entire collection, and departed with his eyes clouded over.

sentences.zh: 著《五代十國紀年》以擬《十六國春秋》，又采太古以來至周威烈王時事，《史記》、《左氏傳》所不載者，為《通鑒外紀》。
