translations.literal: He wrote "Annals of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms" to emulate "Spring and Autumn of the Sixteen Kingdoms," and also gathered from deepest antiquity down to King Weilie of Zhou events not recorded in the Records of the Historian and the Zuo Tradition, compiling "Outer Annals of the Comprehensive Mirror."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Annals of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms to emulate Spring and Autumn of the Sixteen Kingdoms, and also gathered events from deepest antiquity down to King Weilie of Zhou omitted from the Records of the Historian and the Zuo Tradition, compiling them as Outer Annals of the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 家素貧，無以給旨甘，一毫不妄取於人。

translations.literal: His family had always been poor, unable to provide delicacies for parents, and never took a single hair's worth from others without cause.
translations.idiomatic: His family had always been poor and could not provide delicacies for his parents; he never took so much as a single cent from others without just cause.

sentences.zh: 自洛南歸，時方冬，無寒具。

translations.literal: Returning from south of the Luo, it was deep winter and he had no cold gear.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from south of the Luo River, it was deep winter and he had no winter clothing.

sentences.zh: 司馬光遺以衣襪及故茵褥，辭不獲，強受而別，行及潁，悉封還之。

translations.literal: Sima Guang sent him clothes, socks, and old bedding; he declined but could not refuse, was forced to accept and parted; reaching Ying he sealed and returned all.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang sent him clothes, socks, and old bedding. He declined but could not refuse, was forced to accept them and departed; when he reached Ying he sealed everything and sent it all back.

sentences.zh: 尤不信浮屠說，以為必無是事，曰：「人如居逆旅，一物不可乏，去則盡棄之矣，豈得齎以自隨哉？」

translations.literal: He especially did not believe Buddhist teaching, holding such things surely did not exist, and said: "People are like lodging at an inn—not one thing can be lacking; when you leave you abandon everything—how could you carry it along?"
translations.idiomatic: He especially did not believe Buddhist doctrine, holding that such things surely did not exist, and said, "People are like guests at an inn—not one thing can be lacking while you stay. When you leave you abandon everything. How could you carry it all away with you?"

sentences.zh: 好攻人之惡，每自訟平生有二十失、十八蔽，作文以自警，亦終不能改也。

translations.literal: He loved attacking others' faults, often accusing himself of twenty faults and eighteen blind spots in life, writing essays to warn himself—yet in the end could not change.
translations.idiomatic: He loved attacking others' faults, often accusing himself of twenty faults and eighteen blind spots in his life, and wrote essays to warn himself—yet in the end he could not change.

sentences.zh: 死後七年，《通鑒》成，追錄其勞，官其子羲仲為郊社齋郎。

translations.literal: Seven years after death the Comprehensive Mirror was completed; his merit was recorded posthumously and his son Xizhong was appointed suburban-sacrifice attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years after his death the Comprehensive Mirror was completed; his merit was recorded posthumously, and his son Xizhong was appointed suburban-sacrifice attendant.

sentences.zh: 次子和仲有超軼材，作詩清奧，刻厲欲自成家，為文慕石介，有俠氣，亦摎死。

translations.literal: His second son Hezhong had extraordinary talent; his poetry was clear and abstruse; he strove fiercely to form his own school, in prose admired Shi Jie, had chivalrous spirit, and also died young.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Hezhong had extraordinary talent; his poetry was clear and abstruse, and he strove fiercely to form his own school. In prose he admired Shi Jie and had a chivalrous spirit; he too died young.

sentences.zh: 王無咎

translations.literal: Wang Wujiu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujiu

sentences.zh: 王無咎，字補之，建昌南城人。

translations.literal: Wang Wujiu, style name Bu Zhi, was a native of Nancheng in Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujiu, whose style name was Bu Zhi, came from Nancheng in Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為江都尉、衛真主簿、天臺令，棄而從王安石學，久之，無以衣食其妻子，復調南康主簿，已又棄去。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi, served as Jiangdu lieutenant, Weizhen registrar, and Tiantai magistrate, then abandoned office to study with Wang Anshi. Long afterward, unable to feed wife and children, he was reassigned as Nankang registrar, then abandoned that too.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as lieutenant of Jiangdu, registrar of Weizhen, and magistrate of Tiantai, then left office to study with Wang Anshi. After a long interval, unable to support his wife and children, he was reassigned as registrar of Nankang—then abandoned that post as well.

sentences.zh: 好書力學，寒暑行役不暫釋，所在學者歸之，去來常數百人。

translations.literal: He loved books and studied with effort; in heat or cold on journeys he never set them aside. Scholars wherever he went gathered to him—several hundred coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and studied with relentless effort; on journeys in heat or cold he never set his books aside. Scholars wherever he went gathered around him—several hundred at a time coming and going.

sentences.zh: 王安石為政，無咎至京師，士大夫多從之遊，有卜鄰以考經質疑者。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held power, Wujiu came to the capital; many scholar-officials joined him in study; some chose neighboring residences to examine the classics and resolve doubts.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi held power, Wujiu came to the capital, and many scholar-officials joined him in study. Some even chose neighboring residences so they could examine the classics and resolve doubts with him.

sentences.zh: 然與人寡合，常閉門治書，惟安石言論莫逆也。

translations.literal: Yet he seldom harmonized with others, usually shutting his door to work on books; only with Anshi were words in perfect accord.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he seldom harmonized with others, usually shutting his door to work on his books; only with Anshi were his words in perfect accord.

sentences.zh: 安石上章薦其才行該備，守道安貧，而久棄不用，詔以為國子直講，命未下而卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: Anshi memorialized recommending his conduct and ability as comprehensive, adherence to the Way and contentment in poverty—yet long unused. An edict appointed him Erudite of the Directorate of Education; before the order issued he died at forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi memorialized recommending his comprehensive conduct and ability, his adherence to the Way and contentment in poverty—yet he had long gone unused. An edict appointed him Erudite of the Directorate of Education, but before the order was issued he died at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 蔡肇，字天啟，潤州丹陽人。

translations.literal: Cai Zhao, style name Tianqi, was a native of Danyang in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zhao, whose style name was Tianqi, came from Danyang in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 能為文，最長歌詩。

translations.literal: He could write and was especially accomplished in songs and poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He could write, and was especially accomplished in songs and poetry.

sentences.zh: 初事王安石，見器重。

translations.literal: At first he served Wang Anshi and was held in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served Wang Anshi and was held in esteem.

sentences.zh: 又從蘇軾遊，聲譽益顯。

translations.literal: Later he associated with Su Shi and his reputation grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Later he associated with Su Shi, and his reputation grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 第進士，曆明州司戶參軍、江陵推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and served as Mingzhou registrar assistant and Jiangling legal examiner.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served successively as registrar assistant of Ming Prefecture and legal examiner of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，為太學正，通判常州，召為衛尉寺丞，提舉永興路常平。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era he was Erudite of the Directorate of Education, Tongpan of Changzhou, summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Guard, and intendant of Yongxing circuit grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era he served as Erudite of the Directorate of Education and Tongpan of Changzhou, was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Guard, and was made intendant of Yongxing circuit grain transport.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初，入為戶部員外郎，兼編修國史，言者論其學術反覆，提舉兩浙刑獄。

translations.literal: Early in Huizong's reign he entered as Vice Director of the Revenue Ministry, concurrently compiling the national history; critics charged his scholarship was erratic and he was made intendant of judicial affairs in the two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huizong's reign he entered service as Vice Director of the Revenue Ministry, concurrently compiling the national history; critics charged that his scholarship was erratic, and he was made intendant of judicial affairs in the two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 張商英當國，引為禮部員外，進起居郎，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shangying held power he was brought in as Vice Director of Rites, advanced to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and appointed Drafting Attendant within the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shangying held power, he was brought in as Vice Director of Rites, advanced to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and appointed Drafting Attendant within the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 前此，試三題，率以宰相上馬為之候，肇援筆立就，不加潤飾，商英讀之擊節。

translations.literal: Before this, trialing three topics, candidates generally waited on the prime minister's mounting to copy answers. Zhao took brush and finished at once without polish; Shangying read it and beat the table in applause.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, when trialing three topics, candidates generally waited on the prime minister's mounting of his horse to copy his answers. Zhao took up his brush and finished at once without polish; Shangying read it and beat the table in applause.

sentences.zh: 才逾月，以草御史幸義責詞不稱，罷為顯謨閣待制、知明州，言者又論其包藏異意，非議辟雍以為不當立，奪職，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: After barely a month, because a draft reproaching Censor Xing Yi used unsuitable language, he was demoted to Gentleman of the Hall of Displayed Brilliance and prefect of Mingzhou. Critics again charged he harbored contrary intent, disputing the establishment of the Imperial Academy as improper; his post was stripped and he was made intendant of the Cave Heaven Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After barely a month, because a draft reproaching the censor Xing Yi used unsuitable language, he was demoted to Gentleman of the Hall of Displayed Brilliance and prefect of Mingzhou. Critics again charged that he harbored contrary intent, disputing the establishment of the Imperial Academy as improper; his post was stripped and he was made intendant of the Cave Heaven Palace.

sentences.zh: 會赦，復之，卒。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was proclaimed he was restored, then died.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty was proclaimed he was restored to office, then died.

sentences.zh: 李格非

translations.literal: Li Gefei
translations.idiomatic: Li Gefei

sentences.zh: 李格非，字文叔，濟南人。

translations.literal: Li Gefei, style name Wenshu, was a native of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gefei, whose style name was Wenshu, came from Jinan.

sentences.zh: 其幼時，俊警異甚。

translations.literal: As a child he was extraordinarily sharp and alert.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was extraordinarily sharp and alert.

sentences.zh: 有司方以詩賦取士，格非獨用意經學，著《禮記說》至數十萬言，遂登進士第。

translations.literal: The authorities were then selecting candidates by fu poetry; Gefei alone devoted himself to classical learning, composing a Commentary on the Record of Rites of several hundred thousand characters, and thus passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities were then selecting candidates by fu poetry; Gefei alone devoted himself to classical learning, composing a Commentary on the Record of Rites of several hundred thousand characters, and thus passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調冀州司戶參軍，試學官，為鄆州教授，郡守以其貧，欲使兼他官，謝不可。

translations.literal: Posted as registrar assistant in Ji Prefecture, trialed as academic officer, appointed professor at Yan Prefecture. The prefect, seeing his poverty, wished him to hold another office concurrently; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as registrar assistant in Ji Prefecture, trialed as academic officer, and appointed professor at Yan Prefecture. The prefect, seeing his poverty, wished him to hold another office concurrently; he declined.

sentences.zh: 入補太學錄，再轉博士，以文章受知于蘇軾。

translations.literal: He entered to fill a post as Recorder of the Directorate of Education, twice promoted to Erudite, and came to be known for his writing through Su Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He entered to fill a post as Recorder of the Directorate of Education, was twice promoted to Erudite, and came to be known for his writing through Su Shi.

sentences.zh: 常著《洛陽名園記》，謂「洛陽之盛衰，天下治亂之候也」。

translations.literal: He often wrote Record of Famous Gardens of Luoyang, stating that "the rise and fall of Luoyang is the barometer of order and disorder under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He often wrote Record of Famous Gardens of Luoyang, stating that "the rise and fall of Luoyang is the barometer of order and disorder under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 其後洛陽陷於金，人以為知言。

translations.literal: Later Luoyang fell to the Jin; men considered him prescient.
translations.idiomatic: Later Luoyang fell to the Jin; men considered him prescient.

sentences.zh: 紹聖立局編元祐章奏，以為檢討，不就，戾執政意，通判廣信軍。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng era a bureau was established to compile Yuanyou memorials; he was named collator but did not accept, offending those in power, and was made Tongpan of Guangxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era a bureau was established to compile Yuanyou memorials; he was named collator but did not accept, offending those in power, and was made Tongpan of Guangxin Army.

sentences.zh: 有道士說人禍福或中，出必乘車，氓俗信惑，格非遇之途，叱左右取車中道士來，窮治其奸，杖而出諸境。

translations.literal: A Daoist priest who told fortunes sometimes hit the mark always went out in a carriage; the populace believed and were deluded. Gefei met him on the road, ordered attendants to take the priest from the carriage, investigated his fraud thoroughly, beat him, and expelled him beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist priest who told people's fortunes sometimes hit the mark and always went out in a carriage; the populace believed and were deluded. Gefei met him on the road, ordered his attendants to take the priest from the carriage, investigated his fraud thoroughly, beat him, and expelled him beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 召為校書郎，遷著作佐郎、禮部員外郎，提點京東刑獄，以黨籍罷，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: Summoned as Proofreader, promoted to Assistant Compiler and Vice Director of Rites, intendant of judicial affairs in the eastern capital region; dismissed on party rolls, died at sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Proofreader, promoted to Assistant Compiler and Vice Director of Rites, and made intendant of judicial affairs in the eastern capital region; dismissed on party rolls, he died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 格非苦心工於詞章，陵轢直前，無難易可否，筆力不少滯。

translations.literal: Gefei labored at his craft in lyric prose, pressing forward relentlessly without regard to difficulty, ease, or feasibility—his brush never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Gefei labored at his craft in lyric prose, pressing forward relentlessly without regard to difficulty, ease, or feasibility—his brush never slackened.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「文不可以苟作，誠不著焉，則不能工。

translations.literal: He once said: "Literature cannot be written perfunctorily; where sincerity does not show, the work cannot be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Literature cannot be written perfunctorily; where sincerity does not show, the work cannot be accomplished.

sentences.zh: 且晉人能文者多矣，至劉伯倫《酒德頌》、陶淵明《歸去來辭》，字字如肺肝出，遂高步晉人之上，其誠著也。」

translations.literal: And: "Jin men who could write were many, yet reaching Liu Bolun's Ode on the Virtue of Wine or Tao Yuanming's Return, every word seems to issue from lungs and liver, and they stride above other Jin writers—their sincerity shows."
translations.idiomatic: And: "Men of the Jin who could write were many, yet when one reaches Liu Bolun's Ode on the Virtue of Wine or Tao Yuanming's Return, every word seems to issue from the lungs and liver, and they stride above other Jin writers—their sincerity shows."

sentences.zh: 女 清照

translations.literal: Daughter Qingzhao
translations.idiomatic: Daughter Qingzhao

sentences.zh: 妻王氏，拱辰孫女，亦善文。

translations.literal: His wife was of the Wang clan, granddaughter of Gongchen, and she too excelled at writing.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was of the Wang clan, granddaughter of Gongchen, and she too excelled at writing.

sentences.zh: 女清照，詩文尤有稱于時，嫁趙挺之之子明誠，自號易安居士。

translations.literal: His daughter Qingzhao was especially renowned in her day for poetry and prose; she married Zhao Mingcheng, son of Zhao Tingzhi, and styled herself Lady An Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Qingzhao was especially renowned in her day for poetry and prose; she married Zhao Mingcheng, son of Zhao Tingzhi, and styled herself Lady An Yi.

sentences.zh: 呂南公

translations.literal: Lu Nangong
translations.idiomatic: Lu Nangong

sentences.zh: 呂南公，字次儒，建昌南城人。

translations.literal: Lu Nangong, style name Ciru, was a native of Nancheng in Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Nangong, whose style name was Ciru, came from Nancheng in Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 於書無所不讀，于文不肯綴緝陳言。

translations.literal: He read every sort of book; in writing he would not patch together worn phrases.
translations.idiomatic: He read every sort of book; in writing he would not patch together worn phrases.

sentences.zh: 熙甯中，士方推崇馬融、王肅、許慎之業，剽掠補拆臨摹之藝大行，南公度不能逐時好，一試禮闈不偶，退築室灌園，不復以進取為意。

translations.literal: In the Xining era scholars prized the learning of Ma Rong, Wang Su, and Xu Shen; arts of plundering, mending, splitting, and copying flourished. Nangong judged he could not chase the fashion; one attempt at the civil-service examinations failed, so he retired to build a lodge and tend a garden, no longer aiming at advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xining era scholars prized the learning of Ma Rong, Wang Su, and Xu Shen; the arts of plundering, mending, splitting, and copying flourished. Nangong judged that he could not chase the fashion; one attempt at the civil-service examinations failed, so he retired to build a lodge and tend a garden, no longer aiming at advancement.

sentences.zh: 益著書，且借史筆以褒善貶惡，遂以「袞斧」名所居齋。

translations.literal: He wrote all the more, and on the model of the historiographer's brush to praise good and condemn evil, hence named his studio Imperial Robe and Axe.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote all the more, and on the model of the historiographer's brush to praise good and condemn evil, hence named his studio Imperial Robe and Axe.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂士必不得已於言，則文不可以不工，蓋意有餘而文不足，則如吃人之辨訟，必未始不虛，理未始不直，然而或屈者，無助於辭而已。

translations.literal: He once said that if a gentleman must resort to words, then literature cannot be unaccomplished: where thought overflows but words fall short, it is like a stammerer's lawsuit—never without some falsehood, never without some justice, yet sometimes defeated, simply for lack of aid in rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that if a gentleman must resort to words, then literature cannot be unaccomplished: where thought overflows but words fall short, it is like a stammerer's lawsuit—never without some falsehood, never without some justice, yet sometimes defeated, simply for lack of aid in rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 觀書契以來，特立之士，未有不善於文者。

translations.literal: Looking from the age of written contracts onward, men who stood apart have never been poor at writing.
translations.idiomatic: Looking from the age of written contracts onward, men who stood apart have never been poor at writing.

sentences.zh: 士無志於立則已，必有志焉，則文何可以卑賤而為之？

translations.literal: If a gentleman has no ambition to establish himself, so be it; but if he has ambition, how can literature be made meanly?
translations.idiomatic: If a gentleman has no ambition to establish himself, so be it; but if he has ambition, how can literature be made meanly?

sentences.zh: 故毅然盡心，思欲與古人並。

translations.literal: Therefore he resolved wholeheartedly, thinking to stand alongside the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he resolved wholeheartedly, thinking to stand alongside the ancients.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，立十科薦士，中書舍人曾肇上疏，稱其讀書為文，不事俗學，安貧守道，志希古人，堪充師表科，一時廷臣亦多稱之。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanyou, when the ten categories for recommending scholars were established, Drafting Attendant Zeng Zhao memorialized, praising that in reading and writing he shunned vulgar learning, kept poverty and held the Way, his ambition aspiring to the ancients—fit for the Exemplary Teacher category; court officials at the time also praised him widely.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou, when the ten categories for recommending scholars were established, Drafting Attendant Zeng Zhao memorialized, praising that in reading and writing he shunned vulgar learning, kept poverty and held the Way, his ambition aspiring to the ancients—fit for the Exemplary Teacher category; court officials at the time also praised him widely.

sentences.zh: 議欲命以官，未及而卒。

translations.literal: Discussion was underway to appoint him to office, but before the order came he died.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion was underway to appoint him to office, but before the order came he died.

sentences.zh: 遺文曰《灌園先生集》，傳於世。

translations.literal: His posthumous writings are titled Collected Works of the Garden Master, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous writings are titled Collected Works of the Garden Master and have been transmitted in the world.

sentences.zh: 郭祥正

translations.literal: Guo Xiangzheng
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiangzheng

sentences.zh: 郭祥正，字功父，太平州當塗人，母夢李白而生。

translations.literal: Guo Xiangzheng, style name Gongfu, was a native of Dangtu in Taiping Prefecture; his mother dreamed of Li Bai and bore him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiangzheng, whose style name was Gongfu, came from Dangtu in Taiping Prefecture; his mother dreamed of Li Bai and bore him.

sentences.zh: 少有詩聲，梅堯臣方擅名一時，見而歎曰：「天才如此，真太白後身也！」

translations.literal: Young he had a poetic reputation; Mei Yaochen then dominated the age alone. Seeing him he sighed: "Genius such as this—truly a reincarnation of Taibai!"
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had a poetic reputation; Mei Yaochen then dominated the age alone. Seeing him, he sighed, "Genius such as this—truly a reincarnation of Taibai!"

sentences.zh: 舉進士，熙甯中，知武岡縣，簽書保信軍節度判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi; in the Xining era he was magistrate of Wugang County and signed as military coordinator for Baixin Army.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination; in the Xining era he was magistrate of Wugang County and signed as military coordinator for Baixin Army.

sentences.zh: 時王安石用事，祥正奏乞天下大計專聽安石處畫，有異議者，雖大臣亦當屏黜。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held power, Xiangzheng memorialized asking that the empire's grand strategy be entrusted entirely to Anshi's planning, and that dissenters—even grand ministers—be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi held power, Xiangzheng memorialized asking that the empire's grand strategy be entrusted entirely to Anshi's planning, and that dissenters—even grand ministers—be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 神宗覽而異之，一日問安石曰：「卿識郭祥正乎？

translations.literal: The emperor read it and was struck; one day he asked Anshi: "Do you know Guo Xiangzheng?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and was struck; one day he asked Anshi, "Do you know Guo Xiangzheng?

sentences.zh: 其才似可用。」

translations.literal: His talent seems usable."
translations.idiomatic: His talent seems usable."

sentences.zh: 出其章以示安石，安石恥為小臣所薦，因極口陳其無行。

translations.literal: The emperor produced the memorial for Anshi; Anshi was ashamed to be recommended by a petty official and therefore spoke at length of his want of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor produced the memorial for Anshi; Anshi was ashamed to be recommended by a petty official and therefore spoke at length of his want of conduct.

sentences.zh: 時祥正從章惇察訪辟，聞之，遂以殿中丞致仕。

translations.literal: At the time Xiangzheng was following Zhang Dun on an investigative commission; hearing this, he resigned as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiangzheng was following Zhang Dun on an investigative commission; hearing this, he resigned as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後復出，通判汀州。

translations.literal: Later he came out again as Tongpan of Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he came out again as Tongpan of Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知端州，又棄去，隱于縣青山，卒。

translations.literal: As prefect of Duan he abandoned the post again, retired to Green Mountain in the county, and died.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Duan he abandoned the post again, retired to Green Mountain in the county, and died.

sentences.zh: 米芾，字元章，吳人也。

translations.literal: Mi Fu, style name Yuanzhang, was a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Fu, whose style name was Yuanzhang, was a man of Wu.

sentences.zh: 以母侍宣仁後藩邸舊恩，補浛光尉。

translations.literal: Through his mother's service in the old household of Empress Dowager Xuanren in the princely residence, he was appointed district captain of Hangguang.
translations.idiomatic: Through his mother's service in the old household of Empress Dowager Xuanren in the princely residence, he was appointed district captain of Hangguang.

sentences.zh: 曆知雍丘縣、漣水軍，太常博士，知無為軍，召為書畫學博士，賜對便殿，上其子友仁所作《楚山清曉圖》，擢禮部員外郎，出知淮陽軍。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Yongqiu and Lianshui Army, Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, prefect of Wuwei Army, was summoned as Erudite of the Painting Academy, granted audience in the side hall, presented his son Youran's Dawn over the Chu Mountains, was promoted to Vice Director of Rites, and went out as prefect of Huaiyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as magistrate of Yongqiu and Lianshui Army, Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and prefect of Wuwei Army; was summoned as Erudite of the Painting Academy; was granted audience in the side hall and presented his son Youran's Dawn over the Chu Mountains; was promoted to Vice Director of Rites; and went out as prefect of Huaiyang Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: He died at forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 芾為文奇險，不蹈襲前人軌轍。

translations.literal: Fu's writing was singular and perilous, not treading in the tracks of predecessors.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's writing was singular and perilous, not treading in the tracks of predecessors.

sentences.zh: 特妙于翰墨，沈著飛翥，得王獻之筆意。

translations.literal: He was especially marvelous at brushwork—grave yet soaring, capturing Wang Xianzhi's brush intention.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially marvelous at brushwork—grave yet soaring, capturing Wang Xianzhi's brush intention.

sentences.zh: 畫山水人物，自名一家，尤工臨移，至亂真不可辨。

translations.literal: In landscape and figures he formed a school of his own, especially skilled at copying, to the point that true and false could not be told apart.
translations.idiomatic: In landscape and figures he formed a school of his own, especially skilled at copying, to the point that true and false could not be told apart.

sentences.zh: 精于鑒裁，遇古器物書畫則極力求取，必得乃已。

translations.literal: Expert in appraisal; encountering antiquities, books, or paintings he strove with utmost effort to obtain them, stopping only when he had them.
translations.idiomatic: Expert in appraisal, whenever he encountered antiquities, books, or paintings he strove with utmost effort to obtain them, stopping only when he had them.

sentences.zh: 王安石嘗摘其詩句書扇上，蘇軾亦喜譽之。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi once copied out his verses on a fan; Su Shi too praised him with pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi once copied out his verses on a fan; Su Shi too praised him with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 冠服效唐人，風神蕭散，音吐清暢，所至人聚觀之。

translations.literal: His hat and robes imitated Tang style; his bearing was remote and loose, his utterance clear and fluent—wherever he went people gathered to watch.
translations.idiomatic: His hat and robes imitated Tang style; his bearing was remote and loose, his utterance clear and fluent—wherever he went people gathered to watch.

sentences.zh: 而好潔成癖，至不與人同巾器。

translations.literal: Yet fastidiousness became a compulsion, to the point that he would not share towel or vessel with others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fastidiousness became a compulsion, to the point that he would not share towel or vessel with others.

sentences.zh: 所為譎異，時有可傳笑者。

translations.literal: What he did was bizarre; often there were things fit for laughter.
translations.idiomatic: What he did was bizarre; often there were things fit for laughter.

sentences.zh: 無為州治有巨石，狀奇醜，芾見大喜曰：「此足以當吾拜！」

translations.literal: At the Wuwei prefectural seat was a huge stone, grotesque in shape; Fu saw it and rejoiced greatly: "This is worthy of my bow!"
translations.idiomatic: At the Wuwei prefectural seat was a huge stone, grotesque in shape; Fu saw it and rejoiced greatly, saying, "This is worthy of my bow!"

sentences.zh: 具衣冠拜之，呼之為兄。

translations.literal: He put on cap and robes and bowed to it, calling it elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He put on cap and robes and bowed to it, calling it elder brother.

sentences.zh: 又不能與世俯仰，故從仕數困。

translations.literal: Again he could not bend with the age, so in office he was often thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: Again he could not bend with the age, so in office he was often thwarted.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉詔仿《黃庭》小楷作周興嗣《千字韻語》。

translations.literal: Once by imperial order he imitated small regular script after the Huangting Scripture to compose Zhou Xingsi's Thousand-Character Prosody.
translations.idiomatic: Once by imperial order he imitated small regular script after the Huangting Scripture to compose Zhou Xingsi's Thousand-Character Prosody.

sentences.zh: 又入宣和殿觀禁內所藏，人以為寵。

translations.literal: He also entered the Hall of Xuanhe to view treasures stored within the palace; people regarded this as favor.
translations.idiomatic: He also entered the Hall of Xuanhe to view treasures stored within the palace; people regarded this as favor.

sentences.zh: 子友仁字元暉，力學嗜古，亦善書畫，世號小米，仕至兵部侍郎、敷文閣直學士。

translations.literal: His son Youran, style name Yuanhui, studied ardently and loved antiquity, and was also skilled at painting and calligraphy; the age called him Little Mi. He served up to Vice Minister of War and Academician of the Hall for Diffusing Culture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youran, whose style name was Yuanhui, studied ardently and loved antiquity, and was also skilled at painting and calligraphy; the age called him Little Mi. He served up to Vice Minister of War and Academician of the Hall for Diffusing Culture.

sentences.zh: 劉詵，字應伯，福州福清人。

translations.literal: Liu Shen, style name Yingbo, was a native of Fuqing in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen, whose style name was Yingbo, came from Fuqing in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，曆莆田主簿、知廬江縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and served as registrar of Putian and magistrate of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served successively as registrar of Putian and magistrate of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，為講議司檢討官，進軍器、大理丞，大晟府典樂。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era he was collator of the Discussion Office, advanced to Director of Armaments and Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and master of music at the Great Accomplishment Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongning era he served as collator of the Discussion Office, was advanced to Director of Armaments and Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and was made master of music at the Great Accomplishment Bureau.

sentences.zh: 詵通音律，嘗上歷代雅樂因革及宋製作之旨，故委以樂事。

translations.literal: Shen was versed in pitch and mode; he once memorialized on the changes in elegant music through the ages and the aim of Song composition, so he was entrusted with music affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was versed in pitch and mode; he once memorialized on the changes in elegant music through the ages and the aim of Song composition, so he was entrusted with music affairs.

sentences.zh: 又言：「《周官》大司樂禁淫聲、慢聲，蓋孔子所謂放鄭聲者。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Grand Music Master in the Offices of Zhou forbade licentious and slow sounds—this is what Confucius meant by banish the sounds of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The Grand Music Master in the Offices of Zhou forbade licentious and slow sounds—this is what Confucius meant by 'banish the sounds of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 今燕樂之音，失于高急，曲調之詞，至於鄙俚，恐不足以召和氣。

translations.literal: Today's banquet music is too high and hurried; the words of the tunes sink to vulgarity—I fear it cannot summon harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Today's banquet music is pitched too high and hurried; the words of the tunes sink to vulgarity—I fear it cannot summon harmonious qi.

sentences.zh: 宋，火德也，音尚徵，徵調不可闕。

translations.literal: Song is the virtue of Fire; tones should honor zhi mode, and the zhi mode must not be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Song is the virtue of Fire; tones should honor the zhi mode, and the zhi mode must not be lacking.

sentences.zh: 臣按古制，旋十二宮以七聲，得正徵一調，惟陛下才取。」

translations.literal: Your servant, following ancient regulations, rotates the twelve palaces with the seven tones, obtaining one correct zhi mode—may Your Majesty with your talent select it."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, following ancient regulations, rotates the twelve palaces with the seven tones and obtains one correct zhi mode—may Your Majesty with your talent select it."

sentences.zh: 徽宗曰：「卿言是也，五聲闕一不可，《徵招》、《角招》為君臣相說之樂，此朕所欲聞而無言者，卿宜為朕典司之。」

translations.literal: Huizong said: "Your words are right; of the five tones none may be lacking. Summons of the Zhi and Summons of the Jiao are music for ruler and minister to rejoice together—what I wished to hear but had no words for; you should oversee it for Us."
translations.idiomatic: Huizong said, "Your words are right; of the five tones none may be lacking. Summons of the Zhi and Summons of the Jiao are music for ruler and minister to rejoice together—what I wished to hear but had no words for; you should oversee it for Us."

sentences.zh: 他日，禁中出古鐘二，詔執政召詵按於都堂，詵曰：「此與今太簇、大呂聲協。」

translations.literal: Another day, two ancient bells were brought from within the palace; the edict summoned the chief ministers and Shen to examine them in the main hall. Shen said: "These harmonize with today's Taicu and Dalü pitches."
translations.idiomatic: Another day, two ancient bells were brought from within the palace; the edict summoned the chief ministers and Shen to examine them in the main hall. Shen said, "These harmonize with today's Taicu and Dalü pitches."

sentences.zh: 命取大晟鐘扣之，果應。

translations.literal: Ordered to strike the Great Accomplishment bells—they responded as predicted.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to strike the Great Accomplishment bells, they responded as predicted.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「鐘擊之無餘韻，不如石聲，《詩》所雲'依我磬聲'者，言其清而定也。

translations.literal: He also said: "When bells are struck there is no lingering resonance, unlike stone sound; as the Odes says, 'listen to my sounding-stone'—meaning clarity and steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When bells are struck there is no lingering resonance, unlike stone sound; as the Odes says, 'listen to my sounding-stone'—meaning clarity and steadiness.

sentences.zh: 復取以合之，聲益諧。

translations.literal: Again took them to combine them; the sound grew ever more harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He had them struck again together, and the tones harmonized still more perfectly.

sentences.zh: 曆宗正、鴻臚、衛尉、太常寺少卿，纂《續因革禮》，卒。

translations.literal: Served successively as Vice Director of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan, of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; compiled Continuation of Reforms in Ritual; died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through vice-directorships of the imperial clan bureau, diplomatic reception, the imperial stud, and imperial sacrifices, compiled the Continuation of Reforms in Ritual, and died.

sentences.zh: 詵居母喪盡禮，有雙芝生墓側，人以為孝感。

translations.literal: When Shen observed mourning for his mother with full propriety, twin lingzhi grew beside the tomb; people considered it filial response.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen observed his mother's mourning with full propriety, twin lingzhi fungi appeared beside the tomb—people took it as a mark of filial devotion moved by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 倪濤，字巨濟，廣德軍人。

translations.literal: Ni Tao, style Juji, was a man of Guangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Tao, style Juji, was a native of Guangde Army.

sentences.zh: 丱角能屬文，博學強記。

translations.literal: From childhood he could compose prose; broadly learned, powerful memory.
translations.idiomatic: Even in childhood he could compose prose, and he was broadly learned with a powerful memory.

sentences.zh: 年十五，試太學第一，遂擢進士，調廬陵尉、信陽軍教授。

translations.literal: At age fifteen, tested first in the Imperial University, then selected jinshi, appointed Luling assistant magistrate and Xinyang Circuit instructor.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he ranked first in the Imperial University examination, was then selected as jinshi, and was appointed Luling assistant magistrate and Xinyang Circuit instructor.

sentences.zh: 入為太學正，秘書省校書郎、著作佐郎，司勳、左司員外郎。

translations.literal: Entered as Director of the Imperial University, Secretariat collator, Assistant in the Compilation Bureau, outer-section director in the Ministry of Personnel and in the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Director of the Imperial University, Secretariat collator, and Assistant in the Compilation Bureau, and served as outer-section director in the Ministry of Personnel and in the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議有事燕雲，大臣爭先決策，為固位計，皆心知不可，無敢一出口，濤獨言其非。

translations.literal: The court debated action in Yan-Yun; great ministers raced to decide first to secure their posts; all knew in heart it could not be done, none dared speak one word—Tao alone said it was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated action in Yan-Yun, great ministers raced to decide first to secure their posts; all knew in their hearts it was wrong yet none dared speak—Tao alone said it was mistaken.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「景德以來，遼守約不犯邊，盟誓固在，不可渝也。

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "Since the Jingde era the Liao have kept the treaty and not violated the border; the sworn alliance still stands and cannot be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he said, "Since the Jingde era the Liao have kept the treaty and not violated the border; the sworn alliance still stands and must not be broken.

sentences.zh: 天下久平，士不習戰，軍儲又屈，毋輕議以詒後患。」

translations.literal: The realm has long been at peace; scholars are unused to war, and military stores are strained—do not lightly debate this and bequeath trouble to posterity."
translations.idiomatic: The realm has long been at peace; scholars are unused to war, and military stores are strained—do not lightly debate this and bequeath trouble to posterity."

sentences.zh: 王黼怒曰：「君敢沮軍事邪！」

translations.literal: Wang Fu angrily said: "Sir, you dare obstruct the military campaign!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu angrily said, "Sir, you dare obstruct the military campaign!"

sentences.zh: 於是言者論其鼓唱撰造，貶監朝城縣酒稅，再徙茶陵船場，卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: Thereupon critics accused him of agitating and fabricating slander; he was demoted to supervise wine tax at Chaocheng County, then transferred again to the Chaoling shipping station, and died at thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon critics accused him of agitating and fabricating slander; he was demoted to supervise wine tax at Chaocheng County, then transferred again to the Chaoling shipping station, and died at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 死之明年，金人犯闕，朝廷憶濤言，官其一子。

translations.literal: The year after his death the Jurchens assaulted the capital; the court recalled Tao's words and appointed one of his sons to office.
translations.idiomatic: The year after his death the Jurchens assaulted the capital; the court recalled Tao's words and appointed one of his sons to office.

sentences.zh: 有《雲陽集》傳於世。

translations.literal: His Cloud Yang Collection circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Cloud Yang Collection circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 李公麟

translations.literal: Li Gonglin
translations.idiomatic: Li Gonglin

sentences.zh: 李公麟，字伯時，舒州人。

translations.literal: Li Gonglin, style Boshi, was a man of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gonglin, style Boshi, was a native of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，曆南康、長垣尉，泗州錄事參軍，用陸佃薦，為中書門下後省冊定官、御史檢法。

translations.literal: Placed as jinshi; served as assistant magistrate of Nankang and Changyuan, recording secretary of Sizhou; on Lu Dian's recommendation was made collation officer of the Rear Secretariat and investigation officer under the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He placed as jinshi, served as assistant magistrate of Nankang and Changyuan and as recording secretary of Sizhou, and on Lu Dian's recommendation was made collation officer of the Rear Secretariat and investigation officer under the censorate.

sentences.zh: 好古博學，長於詩，多識奇字，自夏、商以來鐘、鼎、尊、彝，皆能考定世次，辨測款識，聞一妙品，雖捐千金不惜。

translations.literal: Fond of antiquity and broadly learned, skilled in poetry, knowing many rare characters; from Xia and Shang down, bells, tripods, wine vessels, and ritual bronzes—he could fix their chronological sequence and decipher inscriptions; hearing of a fine piece, he would not spare a thousand gold.
translations.idiomatic: Fond of antiquity and broadly learned, he was skilled in poetry and knew many rare characters; from Xia and Shang down, bells, tripods, wine vessels, and ritual bronzes—he could fix their chronological sequence and decipher inscriptions, and hearing of a fine piece he would not spare a thousand in gold.

sentences.zh: 紹聖末，朝廷得玉璽，下禮官諸儒議，言人人殊。

translations.literal: Near the end of Shaosheng, the court obtained a jade seal; it was sent down to the ritual officials and various scholars for debate, and each man's words differed.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Shaosheng, the court obtained a jade seal and sent it down to the ritual officials and various scholars for debate, but each man's words differed.

sentences.zh: 公麟曰：「秦璽用藍田玉，今玉色正青，以龍蚓鳥魚為文，著'帝王受命之符'，玉質堅甚，非昆吾刀、蟾肪不可治，琱法中絕，此真秦李斯所為不疑。」

translations.literal: Gonglin said: "The Qin seal used Lantian jade; today's jade color is pure green, with dragon, earthworm, bird, and fish patterns, bearing the inscription 'the talisman of the emperor and king receiving the Mandate'; the jade substance is extremely hard—only the Kunwu blade or toad-fat could work it; the carving method is obsolete—this is truly Qin Li Si's work without doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Gonglin said, "The Qin seal used Lantian jade; today's jade color is pure green, with dragon, earthworm, bird, and fish patterns, bearing the inscription 'the talisman of the emperor and king receiving the Mandate'; the jade substance is extremely hard—only the Kunwu blade or toad-fat technique could work it; the carving method is obsolete—this is truly the work of Qin's Li Si, without doubt."

sentences.zh: 議由是定。

translations.literal: The debate was settled thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The debate was settled thereby.

sentences.zh: 元符三年，病痹，遂致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfu he fell ill with paralysis and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfu he fell ill with paralysis and resigned from office.

sentences.zh: 既歸老，肆意于龍眠山岩壑間。

translations.literal: After returning in old age he roamed freely among the cliffs and ravines of Longmian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After returning in old age he roamed freely among the cliffs and ravines of Longmian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 雅善畫，自作《山莊圖》，為世寶。

translations.literal: He excelled at painting; his self-painted Mountain Villa scroll was a treasure of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at painting; his self-painted Mountain Villa scroll was a treasure of the age.

sentences.zh: 傳寫人物尤精，識者以為顧愷之、張僧繇之亞。

translations.literal: His figure painting in particular was masterly; connoisseurs held him second only to Gu Kaizhi and Zhang Sengyou.
translations.idiomatic: His figure painting in particular was masterly; connoisseurs held him second only to Gu Kaizhi and Zhang Sengyou.

sentences.zh: 襟度超軼，名士交譽之，黃庭堅謂其風流不減古人，然因畫為累，故世但以藝傳雲。

translations.literal: His bearing and breadth surpassed the common run; eminent men praised him together, and Huang Tingjian said his elegance was not less than the ancients—yet because painting weighed on him, the world passes down only his art.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing and breadth surpassed the common run; eminent men praised him together, and Huang Tingjian said his elegance was not less than the ancients—yet because painting weighed on him, the world passes down only his art.

sentences.zh: 周邦彥

translations.literal: Zhou Bangyan
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bangyan

sentences.zh: 周邦彥，字美成，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Zhou Bangyan, style Meicheng, was a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bangyan, style Meicheng, was a native of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 疏雋少檢，不為州裏推重，而博涉百家之書。

translations.literal: Unconventional and little restrained, not esteemed by his prefecture, yet he ranged through the writings of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Unconventional and little restrained, he was not esteemed by his prefecture, yet he ranged through the writings of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，游京師，獻《汴都賦》余萬言，神宗異之，命侍臣讀于邇英閣，召赴政事堂，自太學諸生一命為正，居五歲不遷，益盡力於辭章。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanfeng era he traveled to the capital and presented his Ode to the Bian Capital of more than ten thousand characters; Shenzong was struck by it, ordered attendants to read it in the Erying Pavilion, summoned him to the Secretariat Chancellery, and from among ordinary university students promoted him in one step to Director of Studies; for five years he received no further promotion, and threw himself still more into belles lettres.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanfeng era he traveled to the capital and presented his Ode to the Bian Capital of more than ten thousand characters; Shenzong was struck by it, ordered attendants to read it in the Erying Pavilion, summoned him to the Secretariat Chancellery, and from among ordinary university students promoted him in one step to Director of Studies; for five years he received no further promotion, and threw himself still more into belles lettres.

sentences.zh: 出教授廬州，知溧水縣，還為國子主簿。

translations.literal: He went out as instructor in Luzhou, served as magistrate of Lishui County, then returned as registrar of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as instructor in Luzhou, served as magistrate of Lishui County, then returned as registrar of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 哲宗召對，使誦前賦，除秘書省正字。

translations.literal: Zhezong summoned him for audience and had him recite his former ode; he was made Secretariat collator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong summoned him for audience and had him recite his former ode; he was made Secretariat collator.

sentences.zh: 曆校書郎、考功員外郎，衛尉、宗正少卿，兼議禮局檢討，以直龍圖閣知河中府。

translations.literal: He served as collator, outer-section director of the Ministry of Personnel, vice-director of the Court of Imperial Regalia and of the imperial clan directorate, and concurrently note-taker on the Ritual Revision Board; with the office of Bureau of Illustrated Documents Directly in attendance he governed Hezhong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as collator, outer-section director of the Ministry of Personnel, vice-director of the Court of Imperial Regalia and of the imperial clan directorate, and concurrently note-taker on the Ritual Revision Board; with the office of Bureau of Illustrated Documents Directly in attendance he governed Hezhong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徽宗欲使畢禮書，復留之。

translations.literal: Huizong wished him to finish the ritual compendium and detained him again.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong wished him to finish the ritual compendium and detained him again.

sentences.zh: 逾年，乃知隆德府，徙明州，入拜秘書監，進徽猷閣待制、提舉大晟府。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was made prefect of Longde, then transferred to Mingzhou; he entered the capital as Director of the Secretariat, was advanced to Gentleman-in-Waiting of the Splendid Virtue Pavilion, and made supervisor of the Great Accomplishment Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was made prefect of Longde, then transferred to Mingzhou; he entered the capital as Director of the Secretariat, was advanced to Gentleman-in-Waiting of the Splendid Virtue Pavilion, and made supervisor of the Great Accomplishment Music Office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知順昌府，徙處州，卒，年六十六，贈宣奉大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he governed Shunchang prefecture, then moved to Chuzhou, died at sixty-six, posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee Who Upholds the Foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he governed Shunchang prefecture, then moved to Chuzhou; he died at sixty-six and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee Who Upholds the Foundation.

sentences.zh: 邦彥好音樂，能自度曲，制樂府長短句，詞韻清蔚，傳於世。

translations.literal: Bangyan loved music, could compose tunes himself, and wrote long and short ci in the Music Bureau mode—with limpid, elegant rhyme; they circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan loved music, could compose tunes himself, and wrote long and short ci in the Music Bureau mode with limpid, elegant rhyme; they circulate in the world.

sentences.zh: 朱長文

translations.literal: Zhu Changwen
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Changwen

sentences.zh: 朱長文，字伯原，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Zhu Changwen, style Boyuan, was a man of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Changwen, style Boyuan, was a native of Wu in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 年未冠，舉進士乙科，以病足不肯試吏，築室樂圃坊，著書閱古，吳人化其賢。

translations.literal: Before he came of age he passed the jinshi examination in the second rank; because of crippled feet he refused to test for office, built a studio in the Pleasure Garden Ward, and wrote books while examining antiquities—the people of Wu were transformed by his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he passed the jinshi examination in the second rank; because of crippled feet he refused to test for office, built a studio in the Pleasure Garden Ward, and wrote books while examining antiquities—the people of Wu were transformed by his worth.

sentences.zh: 長吏至，莫不先造請，謀政所急，士大夫過者以不到樂圃為恥，名動京師，公卿薦以自代者眾。

translations.literal: Whenever the prefect arrived, all would first call on him to discuss what the government most urgently needed; scholars who passed through were ashamed not to reach the Pleasure Garden—his name stirred the capital, and many ministers recommended him to succeed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the prefect arrived, all would first call on him to discuss what the government most urgently needed; scholars who passed through were ashamed not to reach the Pleasure Garden—his name stirred the capital, and many ministers recommended him to succeed themselves.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，起教授于鄉，召為太學博士，遷秘書省正字。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era he was raised as local instructor, summoned as Erudite of the Imperial University, and promoted to Secretariat collator.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanyou era he was raised as local instructor, summoned as Erudite of the Imperial University, and promoted to Secretariat collator.

sentences.zh: 元符初，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfu he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanfu he died.

sentences.zh: 哲宗知其清，賻絹百。

translations.literal: Zhezong knew his integrity and granted a hundred rolls of silk as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong knew his integrity and granted a hundred rolls of silk as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 有文三百卷，《六經》皆為辨說。

translations.literal: He left three hundred juan of writings; all Six Classics had explications from him.
translations.idiomatic: He left three hundred juan of writings; all Six Classics had explications from him.

sentences.zh: 又著《琴史》而序其略曰：「方朝廷成太平之功，制禮作樂，比靈斯商、周，則是書也，豈虛文哉！」

translations.literal: He also wrote A History of the Qin, and in its preface said in summary: "When the court accomplishes the work of great peace, orders ritual and composes music, matching the numinous glory of Shang and Zhou—then this book will be no empty text!"
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote A History of the Qin, and in its preface said in summary, "When the court accomplishes the work of great peace, orders ritual and composes music, matching the numinous glory of Shang and Zhou—then this book will be no empty text!"

sentences.zh: 蓋立志如此。

translations.literal: His ambition was thus.
translations.idiomatic: His ambition was thus.

sentences.zh: 劉弇，字偉明，吉州安福人。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, style Weiming, was a man of Anfu in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, style Weiming, was a native of Anfu in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 兒時警穎，日誦萬餘言。

translations.literal: As a child he was alert and quick; each day he could recite more than ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was alert and quick; each day he could recite more than ten thousand words.

sentences.zh: 登元豐二年進士第，繼中博學宏詞科。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng he passed the jinshi examination, then also passed the Erudite in Comprehensive Learning and Great Literary Learning examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfeng he passed the jinshi examination, then also passed the Erudite in Comprehensive Learning and Great Literary Learning examination.

sentences.zh: 曆官知嘉州峨眉縣，改太學博士。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Emei County in Jiazhou and was later made Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Emei County in Jiazhou and was later made Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 元符中，有事於南郊，弇進《南郊大禮賦》，哲守覽之動容，以為相如、子雲復出，除秘書省正字。

translations.literal: In Yuanfu, when the southern suburban sacrifice was held, Yan submitted his Great Rites Ode for the Southern Suburb; Zhezong read it and was moved in countenance, thinking Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong had come again—he was made Secretariat collator.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu, when the southern suburban sacrifice was held, Yan submitted his Great Rites Ode for the Southern Suburb; Zhezong read it and was moved in countenance, thinking Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong had come again—he was made Secretariat collator.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，改著作佐郎、實錄院檢討官，以疾卒於官。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne he was made Assistant in the Compilation Bureau and note-taker of the Veritable Records Institute; he died of illness in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne he was made Assistant in the Compilation Bureau and note-taker of the Veritable Records Institute; he died of illness in office.

sentences.zh: 弇少嗜酒，不事拘檢。

translations.literal: Yan from youth loved wine and did not trouble himself with restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Yan from youth loved wine and did not trouble himself with restraint.

sentences.zh: 為文辭剷剔瑕纇，卓詭不凡。

translations.literal: In literary composition he scraped away flaws and defects, standing out with the extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In literary composition he scraped away flaws and defects, standing out with the extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 有《龍雲集》三十卷，周必大序其文，謂「廬陵自歐陽文忠公以文章續韓文公正傳，遂為一代儒宗，繼之者弇也」。

translations.literal: He had thirty juan of the Dragon Cloud Collection; Zhou Bida prefaced his writing, saying "From the time Ouyang Wenzhong of Luling continued the orthodox line of Han Yu in letters and became the Confucian exemplar of a generation, Yan was his successor."
translations.idiomatic: He had thirty juan of the Dragon Cloud Collection; Zhou Bida prefaced his writing, saying, "From the time Ouyang Wenzhong of Luling continued the orthodox line of Han Yu in letters and became the Confucian exemplar of a generation, Yan was his successor."

sentences.zh: 其相推重如此云。

translations.literal: He was esteemed to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: He was esteemed to this degree.
